desc: Amazing Adventures began life as another of Marvel's tried and tested "double feature" comics - in the mold of Tales of Suspense / Tales to Astonish. Its original features were the Inhumans and Black Widow. However, this dual feature lasted only 8 issues, before the headline feature became "Black Bolt and the Inhumans" for a further 2 issues. Then, from the pages of the X-Men (who at this time did not have their own book) came "The Beast", who took center stage for the next 7 issues before super heroes gave way to space fantasy with "War of the Worlds", where the hero Killraven, Warrior of the Worlds, made his debut. His series filled in the remaining 22 issues of the title.

name: Aquaman
desc: In the aftermath of the JLA arc The Obsidian Age, Aquaman is hated by his former subjects and exiled from the life-giving ocean he once called home. But that doesn't mean his quest to protect the oceans of the world at any cost is over any time soon!

name: Copra
desc:
Note: 

Semi-simultaneously printed as the Image Comics miniseries Death of Copra (#1-4) and the Copra Press series issues #46-49. They are listed on this site under the 'Death of Copra' limited series.

Versions of issue #50 were semi-simultaneously printed by both Image Comics and Copra Press. It is listed with Copra Volume 2 on this site.

name: JSA: Classified
desc: Stories starring the members of the Justice Society of America from throughout their long-standing DCU history! Each arc spotlights members of the team and showcases untold tales from JSA history.

name: Secret Avengers
desc: Who are the Secret Avengers? A new era begins as Marvel's hottest team takes a 21st century twist!

name: Green Lantern
desc:
Series starring the original Green Lantern, Alan Scott.

Note: Indicia title is "Green Lantern Quarterly for #4-18, but is always just "Green Lantern" on cover.

name: Manhunter
desc:
Federal Prosecutor Kate Spencer was the latest hero to use the Manhunter name, as writer Marc Andreyko and penciller Jesus Saiz gave the world a very different take on the hero, with only minor links to those who had gone before.

Kate, a prosecutor, became a ruthless vigilante after watching yet another super powered criminal escape justice - the mutated cannibal known as Copperhead. After Copperhead avoided the death penalty and escaped from police custody, Spencer stole impounded equipment (including a Darkstar powersuit and a staff that chiefly came from 1980's Manhunter Mark Shaw) to help her track down and kill Copperhead. As a chain-smoking mother who put her job before her child, and with a dramatic costume that covered her whole body, this Manhunter was a fresh take on super heroes and gained a loyal following throughout its 38 issue run.

name: Martian Manhunter
desc: The fan favorite team of writer John Ostrander and artist Tom Mandrake fresh off their lengthy run on The Spectre, were ready to take on another caped powerhouse and did so with Martian Manhunter.

name: Moon Knight
desc: Moon Knight's first on-going series. It sets up much of his rogues gallery and delves deeper into Marc Spector and his different personas.

name: Daredevil
desc: THE DEVIL IS REBORN. RENEWED. RESSURECTED. Having turned his world upside down over the past several years, Matt Murdock realizes that justice may not be blind to his past and villains may not be the only ones looking for answers.

name: Doctor Strange
desc:
An All-New All-Different Marvel series!

After the events of Secret Wars, Stephen Strange returns to a world that gravely needs his help.

After issue #26, the Marvel Legacy event starts, in which all of the issues of the previous volume's of Doctor Strange are counted together, making the 27th issue the 381st in total.

name: The Punisher
desc: After the popular The Punisher: Welcome Back Frank mini-series the Punisher received his third mainstream ongoing series. It consists of 37 issues as part of Marvel Knights imprint. Most of the comics in this series are written by Garth Ennis but also Tom Peyer and Steve Dillon. After this series ended, it was replaced with the MAX Comics The Punisher series, which took place in a different reality from the 616 Main Marvel Universe. The Marvel Universe version of the The Punisher would return to a monthly series a few years later in Punisher War Journal Vol. 2.

name: The Question
desc: Series featuring the Question, which began in the late-eighties and continued for 36 issues until it was canceled. It was revived for a single issue, #37, as part of the Blackest Night event.

name: Astonishing Tales
desc: Astonishing Tales is an American anthology comic book series originally published by Marvel Comics from 1970-1976.

name: Avengers
desc: A Marvel NOW! series. Continued from the pages of All-New, All-Different Avengers. After the events of Civil War II, the Avengers regroup once more. After issue 11, the Marvel Legacy event starts, in which all of the issues of the previous volume's of Avengers are counted together, making the 12th issue the 672nd in total.

name: The Avengers
desc:
JED MACKAY AND STORMBREAKER C.F. VILLA TAKE THE REINS OF EARTH'S MIGHTIEST HEROES!

The Star. The Icon. The Witch. The Construct. The God. The Engineer. The King. The world is ever in peril, and a new team of Avengers mobilizes to meet any dangers that dare threaten the planet

name: Captain Marvel
desc:
It ran for 35 issues (plus a Wizard magazine exclusive zero-issue) before being relaunched at #1 again as part of Marvel's 'U-Decide' contest between Captain Marvel, Mar-Ville and Ultimate Adventures.

The whole series has a humorous slant but is still in the traditional cosmic super heroics vein. The full run of the series was written by comics veteran Peter David and the majority of the series was penciled by Chriss Cross.

name: Dark Horse Presents
desc: Dark Horse Presents is an eighty-page, monthly anthology comic published by Dark Horse Comics.

name: Gødland
desc: An American comic book series by Joe Casey and Tom Scioli, set in the Image Universe and published by Image Comics from 2005 to 2012.

name: The Mighty Avengers
desc: As a result of the Initiative after the Civil War, Tony Stark forms a new team of Avengers.

name: Mind MGMT
desc: The story is about Meru, a true crime writer who searches for the truth behind a mysterious airline flight and discovers a secret government agency of super spies, espionage, and psychic abilities. Henry Lyme, the former top agent, has gone rogue and is working to dismantle the organization.

name: Nova
desc: After the events of Annihilation and the Annihilation: Nova mini-series comes a battle-worn Nova with a new attitude as the guardian of the universe. Richard Rider has to find a new balance in his life after the devastating events of Annihilation-Force that changed him forever.

name: Scooby Apocalypse
desc: The comic was conceived by DC Comics co-publisher and artist, Jim Lee, as part of a major reboot using Hanna-Barbera characters, in order to create a new Hanna-Barbera comic book universe.

name: Secret Six
desc: The Secret Six are back in an all-new ongoing series that delivers some of the darkest, most twisted action-adventure the DC Universe has seen since the last time the Secret Six got together!

name: Uncanny X-Men
desc: A Marvel NOW! title. After the conclusion of Avengers Vs. X-Men, the true flagship X-Men title returns! This volume focuses on Cyclops and his group of vigilante mutants.

name: Void Rivals
desc: The series follows Darak and Solila, two individuals from opposing sides of an ancient extraterrestrial racial war, whose ships crash on a barren planet, forcing them to cooperate for survival.

name: X-Men: Blue
desc: After the events of Inhumans v.s. X-Men and X-Men Prime, the team of mutants is reformed and return to greatness. They are divided into two (classic) teams, the Gold team led by Kitty Pryde and the Blue team consisting of the young time-displaced X-Men.

name: X-Men: Gold
desc: After the events of Inhumans v.s. X-Men and X-Men Prime, the X-Men are reformed and return to greatness divided into two (classic) teams, the Gold team led by Kitty Pryde and the Blue team, consisting of the time-displaced X-Men.

name: All Star Western
desc: A "New 52" initiative title starring Jonah Hex among other characters in the wild west period of the DCU. The title was launched by long time writing collaborators Jimmy Palmiotti and Justin Gray.

name: Arion, Lord of Atlantis
desc: Spinning out of the back-up feature in Warlord from Paul Kupperberg and Jan Duursema.

name: Batwing
desc: A New 52 series starring Batman Incorporated member, Batwing, in his own ongoing series.

name: Earth 2
desc: Featuring an alternate earth within the DC Multiverse, Earth 2 is a "Second Wave" title of DC's The New 52 initiative.

name: Ghost Rider
desc: Stars Johhny Blaze as the Ghost Rider as he takes on supernatural threads in a war between Heaven and Hell.

name: Sojourn
desc: The undead warlord Mordath rules the Five Lands with a fist of iron... and sorcery most foul. Fierce and beautiful, Arwyn the archer lost her family to Mordath's unstoppable troll armies. Now Arwyn journeys in search of a mythic hero's arrow of power, the one weapon that can forever end Mordath's reign of fire!

name: Thor
desc: After issue #12, the series reverted back to the numbering of Thor, Volume 1 with issue #600.

name: American Vampire
desc: The series explores notions of vampire evolution and traces the bloodline of a new kind of vampire, an American species, with new powers and characteristics, through various decades of American history.

name: Buffy the Vampire Slayer
desc: After two decades at Dark Horse the Buffy franchise moves to Boom! Studios with an all new series re-imagined under the guidance of Joss Whedon.

name: DV8
desc: The series revolves around the lives of a group of Gen-Active people (Called DV8, or referred to as "The Deviants"), initially living in New York City under the supervision of Ivana Baiul, who sends them on life-threatening black ops assignments.

name: Ultimate Comics X-Men
desc: Iceman, Kitty Pride and the Human Torch discover the true history of the x-gene as the divide between Mankind and Mutantkind grows deeper than ever before! Who are the X-Men and how will they handle the fallout of this universe shattering discovery?

name: Checkmate
desc: Originally a spin-off from the Vigilante series, Checkmate featured the exploits of a super-secret government organization. The Checkmate operatives were known as knights, mortal men, super spies with high tech body suits and gear.

name: Fairest
desc: This series will focus on different characters each arc, the only thing they have in common being that they are female.

name: Howard the Duck
desc: Trapped in a world he never made, the quirky, downright filthy Howard the Duck stars in his own ongoing series!

name: Marvel Spotlight
desc: Marvel Spotlight is a comic book anthology series published by Marvel Comics as a try-out book. It stood out from Marvel's other try-out books in that most of the featured characters made their first appearance in the series. The series originally ran for 33 issues from November 1971 to April 1977.

name: New Avengers
desc: A Marvel NOW! title. To prevent the collision of our Universe with others, the Illuminati, led by Black Panther, must assemble NOW!

name: Descender
desc: A Science fiction/Space opera comic book series written by Jeff Lemire and illustrated by Dustin Nguyen. The series was published by Image Comics. The story follows a young android, TIM-21, trying to survive endless bounty hunters in a universe that has outlawed all robotics and artificial intelligence.

name: Harrow County
desc:
Deep in the hills and hollows of Harrow County dark creatures lurk.  Some of them are forest critters like you'd find in any other place. But some of these critters are more mysterious and more dangerous than most folk might expect. Some you might even call monsters.

When Hester Beck came to the county folks were pleased. She seemed to have power over these monsters and kept them from making mischief. And things seemed to be getting better; the woods a little less scary and the crops a little more hardy. For a time folk turned a blind eye when livestock started dying in Hester's presence. "There must be a trade," they might say. "What is taken must be given." 

But it weren't long before Hester Beck took too much. And that's when the kindly people of Harrow County took Hester's life.

That was 18 years ago...

name: The Losers
desc: Series based loosely off the Golden Age team The Losers, with a new cast and a new story line. It tells about a group of ex-Special Forces who were betrayed while in Iraq and left for dead. Now they want revenge against the man who ordered their deaths....Max.

name: Mighty Samson
desc: A post-apocalyptic adventure, it was set in the area around New York City, now known as "N'Yark", on an Earth devastated by a nuclear war. The series was created by writer Otto Binder and artist Frank Thorne.

name: Mutant X
desc: This series continued directly from X-Factor Vol.1 and focuses on the adventures of X-Man and former X-Factor leader Alex Summers/Havok as he is cast into an alternate time line with no way of returning to his own. Other key players are Bloodstorm, The Brute, The Fallen, Scotty Summers and Madelyne Pryor.

name: Thunderbolts
desc: A new Marvel NOW! ongoing series featuring Red Hulk, Punisher, Flash Thompson as Venom, Red Leader, Deadpool, Elektra, Ghost Rider and Mercy as the all-new Thunderbolts. The series lasted for 32 issues.

name: Titans
desc:
Following the events of Dark Crisis, the Justice League disbanded, and Nightwing officially accepted the responsibility of leading the Titans as Earth's first line of defense.  Based in a new Titans Tower in Blüdhaven, the team - consisting of Nightwing, Starfire, Cyborg, Beast Boy, Raven, Donna Troy, and Roy Harper - faced massive global threats while navigating personal trauma.

Key Story Arcs:
Out of the Shadows: The team establishes their new status quo but is immediately targeted by Amanda Waller and the mysterious Brother Eternity, who uses a humanitarian church as a front for a darker agenda.

Beast World: In a massive crossover event, Beast Boy transforms into "Garro" (a Starro-like entity) to save the world from an alien threat.  However, his spores accidentally turn heroes and citizens worldwide into feral animal hybrids, forcing the Titans to contain their own teammate.

The Dark-Winged Queen: The team deals with the release of Doctor Hate (Raven's demonic side), leading to a spiritual crisis that threatens to tear the group apart.

Terminated: Deathstroke returns with a dangerous new Crime Syndicate (including Clock King and Killer Frost), using his intimate knowledge of the Titans to systematically dismantle them.

DC K.O. (The Finale): The series concludes during the DC K.O. event, where the Titans serve as Earth's final defense against Darkseid's forces and his daughter, Grail, as the planet is nearly transformed into a New Apokolips.

name: Checkmate
desc: Spinning out of the OMAC PROJECT, writer Greg Rucka launches a different spy agency for a different world. Infinite Crisis has changed the world, and Checkmate has shaped its hard-learned lessons into a new game plan. Checkmate holds the line. Cross it, and they'll take you off the board.

name: Harley Quinn
desc: A solo ongoing for Harley Quinn in The New 52. Written by Amanda Conner and Jimmy Palmiotti and illustrated by Chad Hardin.

name: Love Letters
desc: Note: Continues as Love Secrets (1953 series) #32 on-wards. Numbering also continues as Love Letters (1954 series) #32 on-wards.

name: Sex Criminals
desc: Writer Matt Fraction and artist Chip Zdarsky's comedy series about a couple who freeze time when they have sex, then decide to use their powers to commit crimes.

name: Stormwatch
desc: DC Comics announced in June 2011 that the team would be incorporated into the DC Universe in a new series, written by Paul Cornell and drawn by Miguel Sepulveda, as part of the September 2011 relaunch of its comics. Peter Milligan took over the book in issue nine after leaving Justice League Dark with issue eight.

name: Ultimate Comics Spider-Man
desc: Meet Miles Morales, the NEW Ultimate Comics Spider-Man! Following in the footsteps of his predecessor, Peter Parker, Miles prepares for the biggest change of his life! It's the same high-flying adventure you've come to love but with a whole new Ultimate Comics Reborn twist. Power and responsibility take on a whole new meaning in Ultimate Comics Spider-Man!

name: Ultimate Comics: The Ultimates
desc: After the events of the Ultimate Avengers vs. New Ultimates mini-series, The Ultimates return once more, now as part of the "Ultimate Comics" line. Reed Richards has been left for dead following the events of Ultimate Comics Doomsday. Now, with the help and resources of Children of Tomorrow, he vows to solve everything. The republic is burning, and in response to this a new team of Ultimates is formed. The series ended with issue 30 and was continued in the Hunger mini-series and Cataclysm: Ultimates and Cataclysm: The Ultimates' Last Stand mini-series.

name: Captain America
desc: Cancelled series that was continued in the The United States of Captain America mini-series.

name: The Exterminators
desc: An American monthly comic book series, published under the Vertigo imprint by DC Comics. The comic was created by writer Simon Oliver and artist Tony Moore and follows the employees of the Bug-Bee-Gone extermination company. The book is notable for its graphic and darkly humorous take on the extermination business. The first issue was released on January 4, 2006 and the series finished at issue #30, initially been envisioned as a 50-issue series.

name: I Hate Fairyland
desc: The now adult Gert is unable to keep a job, as she lacks any education or skills applicable to the real world. After she is beaten up in a bar and dumped in an alley, a tech billionaire named William Wiggins hires her to find his missing son, who he believes has been taken to Fairyland.

name: Mighty Thor
desc: An All-New, All-Different Marvel series. After the events of Thor Volume 4, Secret Wars and the Secret Wars mini-series Thors, Jane Foster returns to the Marvel Universe in an all-new series. After issue 23, the Marvel Legacy event starts, in which all of the issues of the previous volume's of Thor are counted together, making the 24th issue the 700th in total. After issue 706, the series is revamped with a new number 1 as Thor Volume 5, but also has the Legacy numbering.

name: Nailbiter
desc: The series centers around the fictional town of Buckaroo, Oregon, which has produced sixteen of the United States' worst serial killers, dubbed the Buckaroo Butchers by urban culture.

name: Paper Girls
desc: Paper Girls is an ongoing sci-fi adventure series following four newspaper delivery girls as they wind up in the middle of a time travel mystery.

name: Skullkickers
desc: Two hard-headed mercenaries kill monsters and cause havoc in their search for money, fame and adventure.

name: Uncanny Avengers
desc: After the events of Uncanny Avengers Volume 2 and Secret Wars, a new Avengers and X-Men Unity Squad is formed!

name: The Authority
desc: When the Spirit of the 20th Century formed a team to protect the Earth, people took notice. They can be anywhere on the planet with a moment's thought; speak to cities or the dead; electrocute an entire city block. Despotic rulers, alien invaders and even God must answer to...a higher Authority.

name: The Authority
desc: Dan Abnett and Andy Lanning relaunched the book in May 2008 in the wake of the World's End event and took over the writing duties, accompanied by artist Simon Coleby, writing the first seventeen issues of the series.

name: Green Arrow / Black Canary
desc: This series begins with the GREEN ARROW/BLACK CANARY WEDDING SPECIAL, continues in GREEN ARROW/BLACK CANARY issues #1-29, then concludes with GREEN ARROW (2010) #30-32.

associated.series: Green Arrow / Black Canary Wedding Special (2007)

name: Legion of Super-Heroes
desc: Series was renamed 'Supergirl and the Legion of Super-Heroes' from issues #16-#36 before reverting back to 'Legion of Super-Heroes'.

associated.series: Supergirl and the Legion of Super-Heroes (2006)

name: Savage Avengers
desc: The most savage, most unkillable team of characters in the Marvel Universe is assembled! Wolverine! Venom! Elektra! Punisher! And in their midst – Conan the Barbarian! Conan has returned to the Marvel Universe and his new adventures begin here. What is the City of Sickles? Who is the Marrow God? How is the Hand involved? The roughest and most dangerous characters rumble through this new title starting with...Conan vs. Wolverine? 'Nuff said.

name: Vault of Horror
desc: Was an American bi-monthly horror comic anthology series published by EC Comics in the early 1950s. Along with Tales from the Crypt and The Haunt of Fear, it formed a trifecta of popular EC horror anthologies. The Vault of Horror hit newsstands with its April/May 1950 issue and ceased publication with its December/January 1955 issue, producing a total of 40 issues.

name: Champions
desc: A Marvel NOW! series. From the pages of All-New, All-Different Avengers, the young heroes leave the Avengers to form their own team, the Champions! The series lasted 27 issues and was directly continued into Champions Volume 3.

name: Firestorm the Nuclear Man
desc: The cover title changed to Firestorm the Nuclear Man with issue #50 of The Fury of Firestorm, but the indicia did not change until issue #65. The cover title changed again to Firestorm with #83, but the indicia title did not change until #93.

name: Hawk and Dove
desc: Ongoing Hawk & Dove series following on from the previous year's successes of the 1988 mini-series.

name: Josie
desc:
Numbering continues from She's Josie #16.

Numbering continues with Josie and the Pussycats #45

name: Marvel Treasury Edition
desc: An American comic book series published by Marvel Comics from 1974 to 1981. It usually featured reprints of previously published stories but a few issues contained new material. The series was published in an oversized 10″ x 14″ tabloid (or "treasury") format and was launched with a collection of Spider-Man stories.

name: R.E.B.E.L.S.
desc: Vril Dox finds his authority of L.E.G.I.O.N. usurped a second time. Hunted by the organization he founded, Dox once again assembles a team in hopes of regaining control of L.E.G.I.O.N.

name: Resurrection Man
desc: Mitch Shelley becomes a man who knows death all too well--but only for minutes at a time. Every time he dies, he immediately resurrects, with a different superpower each time! As the Resurrection Man, he searches for clues about his unknown past and the true source of his power.

name: Secret Warriors
desc: Nick Fury has gathered the next generation of super-soldiers to combat HYDRA and other shadowy terrorist threats plaguing the Marvel Universe! Twists and surprises lurk behind every turn for the Secret Warriors!

name: Uber
desc: The series depicts an alternate World War II in which the Third Reich develops powerful superhuman soldiers in 1945, preventing its imminent defeat and forcing the Allied nations to counter with super-humans of their own.

name: Adventure Comics
desc: Join Superboy, Krypto, the Legion of Super-Heroes and more in this series that spans from modern day Kansas to the far flung future and sees the heroes of the DC Universe face off against villains both new and old.

name: American Century
desc: Harry Block, a World War II veteran, fakes his own death and makes his way to Central America to create a new identity for himself as Harry Kraft, a hard-drinking smuggler. During a war in Guatemala, a CIA operative blackmails Block into assassinating Rosa de Santiis, a popular leader in opposition to the CIA puppet dictator General Zavala. Afterward, he heads back to the United States, taking a road trip from Hollywood to Chicago to New York, exploring myriad avenues of 1950s American culture.

name: DC Special Series
desc: Launched as part of the DC Explosion, DC Special Series was anthology that focused on a different character every month.

name: Hawkman
desc: In Hawkman's first solo series, Hawkman and Hawkgirl face menaces including the Shadow Thief and Matter Master, and team up with Adam Strange and Aquaman!

name: Planetary
desc: Planetary is a comic book written by Warren Ellis, drawn by John Cassaday and colored by Laura Martin. Published by the Wildstorm imprint of DC Comics, it was originally supposed to run for 24 issues but instead concluded with the 27th issue.

name: Power Girl
desc: Writers Justin Gray and Jimmy Palmiotti together with artist Amanda Conner emphasized the fun of Power Girl in her first ongoing series. Power Girl had suffered a great deal more than most heroes since her first appearance in All- Star Comics# 58. Originally the cousin of Earth -2's Superman. she had her origins retconned following the "Crisis on Infinite Earth" maxi series to make her the grand daughter of Arion of Atlantis. After the events of "Infinite Crisis" her original Earth 2 Kryptonian origin was back, but the hero now found herself on New Earth - as a new Earth - 2 had its own version of Power Girl.

name: Tales from the Crypt
desc:
An American bi-monthly horror comic anthology series published by EC Comics from 1950 to 1955, producing 27 issues (the first issue with the title was #20, previously having been International Comics (#1–5); International Crime Patrol (#6); Crime Patrol (#7–16) and The Crypt of Terror (#17–19) for a total of 46 issues in the series).

Along with its sister titles, The Haunt of Fear and The Vault of Horror, Tales from the Crypt was popular, but in the late 1940s and early 1950s comic books came under attack from parents, clergymen, schoolteachers and others who believed the books contributed to illiteracy and juvenile delinquency. In April and June 1954, highly publicized congressional subcommittee hearings on the effects of comic books upon children left the industry shaken. With the subsequent imposition of a highly restrictive Comics Code, EC Comics publisher Bill Gaines cancelled Tales from the Crypt and its two companion horror titles, along with the company's remaining crime and science fiction series in September 1954.

name: Top Notch Comics
desc: Note: The hyphen in the cover title does not appear in the title in the indicia.

name: Absolute Wonder Woman
desc: Without the island paradise…without the sisterhood that shaped her…without a mission of peace…what’s left is the Absolute Amazon!

name: Archer and Armstrong
desc: Obadiah Archer was born and raised to cherish three things above all else: the faith of his parents, the love of his 22 brothers and sisters, and his lifelong mission to defeat the ultimate evildoer. Now, after years of training, Archer has been dispatched to the heart of America's festering modern day Babylon, aka New York City, to root out and kill this infamous Great Satan. Unfortunately, dying has never been easy for Archer's target -- the hard-drinking, 10,000-year-old immortal known as Armstrong. Together, this unlikely pair of heroes is about to stumble head first into a centuries-old conspiracy that will bring the whole of ancient history crashing down on the modern day Valiant Universe. And that's going to mean one Hell of a hangover.

name: Batman and Robin
desc: Batman and Robin is an ongoing titled focused on the adventures of Batman (Dick Grayson) and Robin (Damian Wayne). The series commences in the aftermath of the events of Battle for the Cowl, in which Dick Grayson reluctantly takes the cape and cowl, and with it the duties of his former mentor, Batman.

name: Farmhand
desc:
An American comic book created, written, and illustrated by Rob Guillory with help from letterer Kody Chamberlain and colorist Taylor Wells.

In the story, a Louisiana farmer named Jedidiah receives a vision and creates a plant which can grow replacement limbs and organs for human beings. The plot begins several years later when his estranged adult son, Ezekiel, returns home to join the family business. Many outside agents, including foreign and domestic government operatives, are after the secret of Jedidiah's seed. Meanwhile, Jedidiah's former partner, Thorne, has been covertly introducing the seed into the wild and is elected mayor.

name: Low
desc: Ongoing science fiction series from writer Rick Remender and artist Greg Tocchini about a distant future where the surface of Earth has become so irradiated that humanity has receded into cities beneath the ocean in order to survive.

name: Red Hood and the Outlaws
desc: When a shocking encounter with Batman solidifies the Red Hood's status as a villain, Jason Todd goes deep undercover to take down Gotham City's criminal underworld from the inside. Along the way, Jason meets two unlikely allies: a disgraced Amazon warrior named Artemis and a half-baked Superman clone called Bizarro—and the DCU's "Dark Trinity" is born!

associated.series: Red Hood and the Outlaws: Rebirth (2016)

name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Urban Legends
sort_name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Urban Legends
desc:
26 issue series. 

#1-23 reprint issues from the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1996) series at Image Comics. 

Issues #24-26 are original stories written to give proper closure to this series.

name: Uncanny Avengers
desc: A Marvel NOW! title. From the ashes of Avengers Vs. X-Men, an all-new team of Avengers assemble!

name: Untold Tales of Spider-Man
desc: The series was part of an experiment for Marvel, where they published a number of new titles for only 99 cents in the hopes that they would attract new, young readers who might have been put off by the then-U.S.$1.50/$1.95 standard prices for comic books at the time. Uniquely among those titles, Untold Tales of Spider-Man presented new stories set in the early days of Spider-Man's superhero career.

name: What The--?!
desc: A Marvel Comics comic book series self-parodying the Marvel Universe, similar in vein to the 1960s series Not Brand Echh.

name: X-Men
desc: The fourth series to bear the name, starring the first all-female team in X-Men history.

name: X-O Manowar
desc:
Born under the oppressive thumb of the Roman Empire, Aric of Dacia learned warfare at an early age. It was amid such violence that he was abducted by an alien race. Forced into slavery, he survived where others perished. His escape would come from bonding with a weapon of immeasurable power: the X-O Manowar armor. With it, he returned to Earth…only to find himself stranded in the modern day.

But that was a lifetime ago.

Now, far from home on a strange and primitive new world, Aric has begun a new life. Liberated from his past, he tends to his crops. Free from war. Free from violence. Free from the armor.

But the machinery of death marches his way once again. Conscripted into an alien army and thrown into an unforgiving conflict, the fury inside him finds voice as he is forced to embrace the armor once more. With it, he will decimate armies, topple empires and incite interplanetary warfare as he rises from SOLDIER to GENERAL to EMPEROR to VISIGOTH. They wanted a weapon. He will give them war!

name: X-Statix
desc: Peter Milligan and Mike Allred's subversive, media-loving mutants — the world-famous X-Statix — star in a series of bizarre, hilarious and deadly adventures! See all your favorites — including the Orphan, the Anarchist, Dead Girl,

name: Absolute Batman
desc: Without the mansion…without the money…without the butler…what’s left is the Absolute Dark Knight!

name: The Astounding Wolf-Man
desc: A spin-off of Robert Kirkman's Invincible, the series was created and written by Kirkman with art by Jason Howard.

name: Black Panther
desc: An All-New, All-Different Marvel series. In this groundbreaking series, a civil-war rages in Wakanda! After issue 18, the Marvel Legacy event starts, in which all of the issues of the previous volume's of Black Panther are counted together, making the 19th issue the 166th in total.

name: Brightest Day
desc: Once dead, twelve heroes and villains have been resurrected by a white light expelled from deep within the Earth. Called a miracle by many and a sign of the apocalypse by others, the group's rebirth is a complex mystery that each now hopes to unravel--for the sake of the entire DC Universe.

name: B&V Friends Forever
desc: Each issue has a unique subtitle on the cover, and each cover is numbered "1", as if each issue were a one-shot. But in the indicia, the numbers go "1 (#1)", "1 (#2)", "1 (#3)", etc., showing that this is intended as a series.

name: Captain Marvel
desc: This is Captain Marvel volume 6; though it is actually a relaunch/continuation of Captain Marvel vol. 5.

name: Case Files: Sam & Twitch
desc: This is the second spinoff book featuring New York City police detectives Sam Burke and Twitch Williams.

name: Clive Barker's Night Breed
desc: Marvel's adaption of Clive Barker's film, Nightbreed, about a society of monsters that live on the outskirts of society in a place called Midian.

name: Geiger
desc:
Set years after a devastating nuclear war destroys civilization, the story follows Tariq Geiger, a man who was exposed to deadly radioactive fallout while hiding in a fallout shelter to save his family. Transformed into a glowing, superpowered nuclear entity who must wear a containment suit to control his lethal energy, Geiger walks the radioactive wasteland of North America as the Glowing Man, protecting innocent survivors while hunted by brutal warlords seeking his immense power.
Note: Indicia list title as "Geiger (2024)". Since this a bit redundant, we'll be using "Geiger".

name: Ghost Rider 2099
desc: The series is set in the year 2099, in a dystopian possible future of the Marvel Universe, and features Kenshiro "Zero" Cochrane, a hacker who was killed but resurrected as the Ghost Rider — his mind controlling a powerful and well-armed robot. As with most of the Marvel 2099 titles, the protagonist was a futuristic version of a commercially successful Marvel Universe character. The series was heavily influenced by cyberpunk science fiction.

name: Guardians of the Galaxy
desc: After the events of Annihilation Conquest, Star Lord brings together a band of heroes to face the threats no-one else can!.

name: Hourman
desc: The 1999 ongoing series Hourman, spun off from the DC One Million event, stars the android Hourman, the third hero with the name. Written in its entirety by Tom Peyer, the series features Hourman’s quest for humanity, with the helping hand of Justice League mascot Snapper Carr and his ex-wife Bethany Lee.

name: Hunter: The Age of Magic
desc: Series depicts Tim Hunter's final days at the White School and the beginning of his life following graduation.

name: The Invisibles
desc:
The Invisibles is a comic book series published by the Vertigo imprint of DC Comics. It was created and scripted by Scottish writer Grant Morrison, and drawn by various artists throughout its publication.

The series loosely follows the doings of a single cell of The Invisible College, a secret organization battling against physical and psychic oppression using time travel, magic, meditation, and physical violence.

For most of the series, the team includes leader King Mob; Lord Fanny, a transgender Brazilian shaman; Boy, a former member of the NYPD; Ragged Robin, a telepath with a mysterious past; and Jack Frost, a young hooligan from Liverpool who may be the next Buddha. Their enemies are the Archons of the Outer Church, interdimensional alien gods who have already enslaved most of the human race without their knowledge.

name: Justice League Odyssey
desc: Justice League Odyssey is a series taking a group of heroes into the Ghost Sector, a territory populated by worlds that had been bottled up and imprisoned on the planet Colu.

name: The Savage She-Hulk
desc: When criminal defense attorney Jennifer Walters is shot by a mob hitman, her cousin saves her life with a blood transfusion - but that cousin is Bruce Banner, and his gamma-irradiated blood turns her into the Savage She-Hulk! Suddenly she's a mean, green lawyering machine, and criminals the world over had better watch out. Now, experience She-Hulk's adventures from the very beginning! Her quest will take her from the halls of justice to other dimensions and pit her against Iron Man, mind-controlling cults, the Man- Thing, and even her own father.

name: Shadowpact
desc: Join Nightmaster, Ragman, Nightshade, Blue Devil, Enchantress and Detective Chimp — the mismatched magical heroes from DC's DAY OF VENGEANCE— as they take on new strange and magical threats. They might just save the world…if they manage to get along that is.

name: Sons of Anarchy
desc: Initially solicited as a six-issue limited series and then extended to twenty-five issues total.

name: Spider-Man 2099
desc: After the events of Spider-Man 2099 Volume 2 and Secret Wars, Spider-Man 2099 returns in his own new series!

name: Thor: God of Thunder
desc: A Marvel NOW! new ongoing series starring Thor, the God of Thunder. The series is continued from The Mighty Thor (vol. 2). Written by Jason Aaron with art by Esad Ribic, this series received high appraisal for it's story and it's art. It lasted until issue 25, after which the series was revamped as 'Thor Volume 4' staring a new female Thor, still written by the same writer.

name: X
desc: Note: The indicia title of the first issue is "Comics' Greatest World: X," and for the rest of the series it is only "X."

name: Air
desc: Was an ongoing comic book series published by DC Comics as part of the Vertigo imprint. It was created by writer G. Willow Wilson and artist M. K. Perker.

name: Batgirl
desc: In the wake of FINAL CRISIS, a new heroine took on the cape and cowl and mantle of Batgirl: the former vigilante known as Spoiler, Stephanie Brown! But her ascension into the role might not sit well with the other members of the Bat Family!

name: Crimson
desc: A fantasy-horror vampire comic book series created from artist Humberto Ramos and writer Brian Augustyn, from story concepts by Francisco Haghenbeck and Oscar Pinto.

name: Demon Knights
desc: A DC Comics title launched in 2011 as part of that company's line-wide title relaunch, The New 52. It is a team title featuring Etrigan, Madame Xanadu, Shining Knight and others. Its main difference to other team titles, such as the Justice League, is that this team is based in the Medieval period of the DC Universe history.

name: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
sort_name: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
desc: A 24 issue maxi-series adapting the entire text of Philip K. Dick's novel that inspired the movie "Blade Runner."

name: FBP: Federal Bureau of Physics
desc: The title was previously known as Collider, but ran into copyright issues, and had to change its name with the second issue. The first issue of Collider was reprinted as FBP: Federal Bureau of Physics #1 after the release of the second issue.

name: Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man
desc: A comic book series that was published by Marvel Comics. The title is derived from a trademark self-referential comment often made by Spider-Man (as in "just another service provided by your friendly neighborhood Spider-Man!"). The first series began in October 2005 and was primarily written by Peter David.

name: Incredible Hulks
desc: Continued from issue #611 of the Incredible Hulk (2009). The series lasted until issue #635

name: Justice League: Generation Lost
desc: Justice League: Generation Lost is a bi-weekly title written by Judd Winick and drawn by a rotating team of artists which was first published in 2010. The book forms part of DC's multi-title Brightest Day event, with the title focusing on the fall-out of Maxwell Lord's resurrection during the events of Geoff John's Blackest Night arc.

name: Manhunter
desc: The first Manhunter volume starring then new Manhunter Mark Shaw (later known as The Privateer) as he attempts to break away from the Manhunter legacy. Written by John Ostrander and Kim Yale, the series tied in to other Ostrander written titles.

name: Marvel Preview
desc: A black-and-white comics magazine published by Magazine Management for fourteen issues and the affiliated Marvel Comics Group for ten issues.

name: New Excalibur
desc: Captain Britain brings together a new team of Excalibur after the events of House of M.

name: Plop!
desc: A comic book anthology series published by DC Comics in the mid-1970s. It falls into the horror / humor genre. It lasted 24 issues and the series ran from Sept./Oct. 1973 to Nov./Dec. 1976.

name: Stormwatch: P.H.D.
desc:
An American comic book published by Wildstorm comics. It is the fourth volume to bear the name Stormwatch. It was first published in November 2006 and was written by Christos Gage with art by Doug Mahnke.

The series ended after issue #12, but restarted in August 2008 as a part of the World's End event with issue #13.

name: Ultimate Spider-Man
desc: THE NEW ULTIMATE SPIDER-MAN FOR A NEW ULTIMATE UNIVERSE! Visionary writer Jonathan Hickman (HOUSE OF X/POWERS OF X) and acclaimed artist Marco Checchetto (DAREDEVIL) bring you a bold new take on Spider-Man, with this, the debut title of the new line of Ultimate Comics! After the events of ULTIMATE INVASION, the world needs a hero…who will rise up to take on that responsibility? Prepare to be entangled in a web of mystery and excitement as the all-new ULTIMATE SPIDER-MAN comic redefines the wall-crawler for the 21st Century!

name: X-Men Forever
desc: An alternative reality series, that continues the X-Men series from the point when Chris Claremont left the series originally.

name: Amazing Spider-Man: Renew Your Vows
desc: A Marvel NOW! series. From the pages of the alternate reality first seen in Amazing Spider-Man: Renew Your Vows Volume 1, comes an all-new ongoing series!

name: The Batman Chronicles
desc: The Batman Chronicles was a seasonally published collection of three Batman stories per issue, excluding the final four issues.

name: Doctor Who
desc: Reprints the adventures of the Fourth and Fifth Doctor, from Doctor Who Magazine.

name: Eightball
desc: Eightball is a comic book by Daniel Clowes and published by Fantagraphics Books. It ran from 1989 to 2004. The first issue appeared soon after the end of Clowes's previous comic book, Lloyd Llewellyn. Eightball has been among the best-selling series in alternative comics.

name: FF
desc: The World's Greatest Comic Magazine just got greater! A bold new direction for Marvel's First Family featuring new members, old friends, older enemies and uneasy alliances!

name: The Mighty Thor
desc: Written by Matt Fraction and illustrated by Olivier Coipel and started when Thor volume 1 returned to it's original name Journey Into Mystery with issue 622.

name: Ms. Marvel
desc: Ms. Marvel's first ongoing series. It follows the adventures of Carol Danvers after she gained superpowers and became a superhero.

name: Peter Parker: The Spectacular Spider-Man
desc: Peter Parker's world is about to turn upside down! After issue 6, the Marvel Legacy event starts, in which all of the issues of the previous volume's of (Peter Parker) the Spectacular Spider-Man are counted together

name: Sinestro
desc: The greatest Green Lantern turned greatest Green Lantern threat Thaal Sinestro stars in his very own series! He has lost everything he's ever loved: his home, his family, his only friend. But no matter how desperate he becomes, Sinestro will never be without fear.

name: Hawkeye
desc: The legendary superhero during his time when he is NOT being an Avenger. Clint Barton becomes a landlord and a pet owner, but in the process makes some deadly enemies. Plus, can he balance a relationship and a friendship with a certain red-headed Russian spy, ex-wife, and flirtatious femme fatale?

name: House of Whispers
desc:
Twenty-two issue series.

Note: Series was originally cancelled with issue #22 scheduled to be the last issue. However, after the initial cancellation announcement, DC decided to digitally publish issues #21 (on July 2, 2020) and #22 (on July 7, 2020) online, then in print in the third collected edition.

name: Marvel Knights: Spider-Man
desc:
Marvel Knights is an imprint of Marvel Comics that contained standalone material taking place inside the Marvel Universe (Earth-616). The underlying difference between this title and the other Spider-Man titles was that Marvel Knights Spider-Man was done with a more mature slant (in style if not content), thus the "Marvel Knights" prefix.

This series picks up where Sensational Spider-Man Volume 1 left off, and ends in February 2006, with issue #23 renamed to The Sensational Spider-Man Volume 2.

name: The New Archies
desc:
An American animated sitcom produced by DIC Animation City, based upon the characters by Archie Comics.

The series, originally produced for NBC's Saturday morning schedule and broadcast from September 12 to December 5, 1987, depicted the characters of Archie Andrews, Betty Cooper, Veronica Lodge, Jughead Jones, Reggie Mantle, and other students of Riverdale High School as pre-teens in junior high.

name: PunisherMAX
desc: Continued from the MAX Punisher series, Punisher: Frank Castle issue 75. An all-new ongoing series from the acclaimed team of  Jason Aaron and Steve Dillon, the new storytellers behind Marvel's most brutal vigilante. The series lasted until issue 22, after which the story of the MAX version of the Punisher ended.Collected Editions PunisherMAX: Kingpin (#1-5)Punisher Max by Jason Aaron Omnibus (#1-22)Punisher MAX: The Complete Collection Volume Seven (#1-22) PunisherMAX: Bullseye (#6-11) PunisherMAX: Frank (#12-16) PunisherMAX: Homeless (#17-22)Translated into Spanish.

name: Route 666
desc: Tells the story of Cassie, an escaped mental patient who targets seemingly random victims as she drifts across the country. She claims they are monsters, disguised as humans, covertly dwelling among us, and only she can detect them. She claims they steal souls to use for some unknown, unspeakable purpose. She must be a dangerous lunatic, right? But what if she's not?

name: The Transformers: Regeneration One
desc: Regeneration One continues from the Marvel US "The Transformers" (1984) series. This continuity does not include the events of the later Marvel UK "The Transformers" (1984) stories or "Transformers: Generation 2" (1993). The series ended with the intended issue 100.

name: Uncanny Inhumans
desc: Spinning out of the events of the Inhuman ongoing series, this series had a special issue 0 and continued after the events of the Inhumans: Attilan Rising Secret Wars mini-series. This series was accompanied by the Uncanny Inhumans Annual. The series ended with issue 20, after the events of Inhumans v.s. X-Men. David Soule also ended his 4 year run on the various Inhumans series with this volume. The Inhumans' story continued in the Inhumans Prime one-shot and the ongoing Royals series.

name: w0rldtr33
desc: In 1999, a group of young friends discovered the Undernet, a secret architecture hidden beneath the internet that allows users to record, share, and experience pure violence and cruelty. After suffering a traumatic tragedy, they managed to seal it away, vowing never to speak of it again. Decades later, the Undernet re-emerges through a terrifying cyber-entity known as PH34R, spreading extreme violence across the globe and forcing the surviving friends to reunite and confront the digital nightmare they failed to destroy.

name: X-Men The Hidden Years
desc: Series that explores the adventures the original X-men had during the 'gap' of reprint comics between Uncanny X-men issue 67 till issue 93.

name: Absolute Flash
desc: A young Wally West must understand and train with his powers. Unlike most interpretations of the Flash, there is no Speed Force or Flash family, so Wally must learn to use more dangerous powers without any mentors to help him.

name: Avengers World
desc: An All-New Marvel NOW! series. The Avengers go global as the team expands it's territory across the world!

name: Billy Batson and the Magic of Shazam!
sort_name: Billy Batson and the Magic of Shazam!
desc: An all-ages comic book series published by DC Comics as a part of its Johnny DC imprint. The series debuted in September 2008, and was originally written and drawn by Mike Kunkel.

name: Daredevil
desc: An All-New Marvel Now series. The series is a continuation of Daredevil Vol.3 that had the same creative team.

name: Nova
desc: Meet Richard Rider, an ordinary teenager whom comes into the possession of the awesome Nova Force! The first ongoing series starring Nova, the Human Rocket. While the cover title was always The Man Called Nova it wasn't until issued 22 that the indicia changed to The Man Called Nova continuing the series.

name: Real Fact Comics
desc: A series of educational American comic books published by three early iterations of DC Comics: World's Best Comics, Inc., Detective Comics, Inc., and National Comics Publications. The series lasted for 21 issues with cover dates from March/April 1946 to July/August 1949. Like most educational comics besides the Parents' Magazine Institute's flagship series, True Comics, the series suffered from poor sales.

name: Redcoat
desc: British redcoat and all-around rogue, Simon mysteriously became immortal in 1776 after a run-in with the clandestine cabal known as the Founding Fathers, which included George Washington, John Hancock, and many other prominent American Revolutionary War leaders. Since that fateful day, Simon has led a life of adventure and avarice, rubbing elbows (and sometimes fists) with many of history’s most renowned figures, including his nemesis Benedict Arnold, Albert Einstein, Annie Oakley, and many more. One thing they all agree on: they never want to see him again! But what are the true origins and extent of Simon’s power and the mysterious organization behind them? And how has it secretly shaped America and the world? Simon’s on a quest to find out

name: The Sacrificers
desc: In a harmonious and prosperous world, peace is maintained through a terrifying bargain: every family from the lower, impoverished agricultural class must sacrifice one of their children to the god-like high ruling class. The story follows Soluna, the rebellious daughter of the arrogant Sun God, and Pigeon, a quiet bird-like farm boy chosen by his family as a sacrifice, whose intersecting lives threaten to shatter the violent, hidden foundation of their utopian society.

name: X-O Manowar
desc: Seized from the Nazis at the end of WW II, The X-O Armor has been property of the United States government for over 50 years. Decades out of use, its awesome capabilities are a complete mystery. That is until Donovan Wylie, genius of Silicon Valley, steps in and begins to unlock the armor's secrets.

name: All-New X-Men
desc: An All-New, All-Different Marvel series. Continued from All-New X-Men Vol.1. After the events of Secret Wars and Death of X, the time-displaced original X-Men set out to see the world!

name: Archie & Friends
desc: Note: Issues are cover-numbered #1, and the sequence and issue title is in the indicia in parentheses, such as ...Beach Party #1 (#2).

name: The Batman Family
desc: As part of its new 'Giant' line of titles, DC launched 'Batman Family', with its memorable debut of the Robin - Batgirl team.

name: Coffin Hill
desc: COFFIN HILL stars Eve Coffin, a rebellious, teenage lowlife from a high-society family with a curse that goes back to the Salem Witch trials.

name: DC Universe Presents
desc: The premise of the book was similar to that of DC's original Showcase and DC Comics Presents series. It would introduce characters and concepts into the rebooted universe. The final issue of this series, #19, was published in April 2013.

name: Die
desc: A horror/fantasy comic book about role-playing games, influenced by the portal fantasy and LitRPG literary genres, written by Kieron Gillen and illustrated by Stephanie Hans. The series focuses on a group of British adults who are drawn back to an icosahedron-shaped world they originally visited as teenagers; the group left behind a friend upon their original escape and never discussed the experience. It was published by Image Comics and ran for twenty issues, beginning in December 2018 and ending in September 2021.

name: Extraordinary X-Men
desc: After the events of Secret Wars and the Death of X series, the X-Men are reunited in an even more dangerous world.

name: Grayson
desc: Following his public reveal as Nightwing at the hands of the Crime Syndicate during Forever Evil, Dick Grayson fakes his death and becomes an agent of the espionage agency Spyral as an inside man for Batman.

name: Guardians of the Galaxy
desc: Continued from Guardians of the Galaxy Volume 3 and the Secret Wars Guardians of Knowhere mini-series. This volume has the Guardians stranded on Earth after the Second Superhuman Civil War. The series is then continued in All-New Guardians of the Galaxy.

name: I Hate Fairyland
desc: A black comedy fantasy comic written and illustrated by Skottie Young, and published by Image Comics, which started publication in October 2015. The comic follows Gertrude, a woman who was transported to a mystical world called Fairyland as a child. Thirty years later, Gertrude is now an un-aging, violent misanthrope who, alongside her reluctant guide and friend Larry, constantly tries and fails to return to the real world.

name: I, Vampire
desc: A "New 52" title starring vampires Andrew Bennett and his former lover Mary, Queen of Blood.

name: Kill or be Killed
desc: The story is about Dylan, a depressed college student who attempts suicide. He survives due to unlikely events, but is soon visited by a demon who explains he spared Dylan's life. In exchange, Dylan will be allowed to live one more month for every person he kills.

name: Micronauts
desc: Note: Indicia reads "Micronauts Vol. 2", but all the covers for the entire series read, "Micronauts: The New Voyages".

name: Southern Bastards
desc: Earl Tubb is an angry old man with a very big stick. Euless Boss is a high school football coach with no more room in his office for trophies and no more room underneath the bleachers for burying bodies. And they're just two of the folks you'll meet in Craw County, Alabama, home of Boss BBQ, the state champion Runnin' Rebs and more bastards than you've ever seen. A Southern fried crime comic by Jason Aaron and Jason Latour.

name: Strange Tales
desc: This series is a continuation of the Strange Tales series that ended in 1968 with issue 168.

name: That Texas Blood
desc: Set in the sun-baked, desert landscape of Ambrose County, Texas, the story follows aging Sheriff Joe Bob Coates as he confronts the dark and violent underbelly of his rural hometown. Beginning with the return of a troubled man who comes home to settle his deceased brother's affairs, a simple trip plunges the town into a terrifying spiral of murder, old grudges, and criminal conspiracies that test the sheriff's resolve and morality.

name: WildC.A.T.S: Covert Action Teams
desc: Note: Indicia list series as "WildC.A.T.S: Covert Action Teams". First issue indicates three issue mini-series.
Numbering continues from previous Warren series 1984, which was re-titled on a request by the estate of George Orwell.

name: Blood & Thunder
desc:
The story is set in a far-future, multi-tiered society (centered on the asteroid-city Metro-1) where humanity has integrated with various alien species.  The plot follows Akeldama "Blood" Bledsoe, the galaxy's premier bounty hunter, who is distinguished by a floating cloud of actual blood that serves as her "hair."

She is partnered with Thunder, an experimental, sentient, and often frustratingly pacifist A.I. rifle.  The central conflict ignites when a mysterious and ultra-dangerous entity known as Prisoner X escapes from an orbiting maximum-security prison.  As Blood and Thunder pursue the fugitive across strange alien worlds, they discover that the prisoner holds secrets regarding Blood's forgotten past - secrets that the ruling elite of Metro-1 have gone to great lengths to bury.

name: Capt. Savage and His Leatherneck Raiders
sort_name: Capt. Savage and His Leatherneck Raiders
alt_names: Captain Savage and His Battlefield Raiders!
desc:
Note: Title indicia is 'Capt. Savage and His Leatherneck Raiders'.

Issues 1-8: Capt. Savage and His Leatherneck Raiders (cover and indicia title)
Issues 9-14: Captain Savage (indicia title); Captain Savage and His Battlefield Raiders! (cover title)
Issues 15-19: Capt. Savage (indicia title); Captain Savage and His Battlefield Raiders! (cover title)

name: The Huntress
desc: Post-Crisis, the concept of Earth-2 was done away with, meaning the original Huntress, Helena Wayne, was no more. Creators Joe Staton and Joey Cavalieri, who had previously worked on the Helena Wayne version of the character, were tasked with creating a new version. Helena was Now Helena Bertinelli, born into a mafia family which she witnessed being murdered at age 19, setting her out on a one woman war of the mob.

name: I Am Batman
desc: Future State gave readers a preview of things to come with Jace Fox as the new Batman...but his debut in the core line arrives with a bang! Picking up immediately from the events of The Next Batman: Second Son, Jace thrusts himself into action when the Magistrate's crackdown on Alleytown begins, using armor he's found in the abandoned Hibernaculum. The age of a new Dark Knight starts now!

name: Journey into Mystery
desc: Part of a line of science fiction and horror anthologies with more thematic cohesion than the company's earlier attempts that decade.

name: Justice League International
desc: Preceded by Justice League, Continues in Justice League America and Justice League Europe.

name: The New Gods
desc: Jack Kirby's original series featuring the first appearances of Orion, Highfather and Darkseid!

name: Sensational Spider-Man
desc:
The Sensational Spider-Man (vol. 2) is a comic book series starring Spider-Man and published monthly by Marvel Comics for 41 issues between 2004 and 2007. It was originally published under the Marvel Knights imprint (as Marvel Knights Spider-Man, vol. 1, issues #1–22). The underlying difference between this title and the other Spider-Man titles was that Marvel Knights Spider-Man was done with a more mature slant (in style if not content), thus the "Marvel Knights" prefix.

Note: Indicia of #23 shows title to be "Sensational Spider-Man".

name: Silk
desc: An All-New, All-Different Marvel series. After the events of Silk Vol.1 and Secret Wars, Silk returns in her own ongoing series.

name: Star Brand
desc: Note: The Indica title and Cover title change from 'Star Brand' to 'The Star Brand' with issue #11.

name: Winter Soldier
desc: Featuring Winter Soldier and Black Widow, the super-spies of the Marvel Universe! Ex-Russian Sleeper Agents awaken, but under whose control?

name: A+X
desc: Spinning directly out of AVX! Like AVX: VS., this book brings you two stories every month by the industry's top creators!

name: Clean Room
desc: It’s the start of the first Vertigo series from fan-favorite writer Gail Simone, with 2000AD artist Jon Davis-Hunt! Astrid Mueller is the enigmatic and compelling guru of a giant self-help organization—a devastatingly powerful figure in the industry between psychology and religion. Journalist Chloe Pierce’s fiancé decided to pick up Astrid’s book, and within three months he was dead. Something in Astrid Mueller’s book made Philip blow his brains out all over Chloe’s new kitchen.

name: Deadpool Team-Up
desc: Note: Series begins with the giant-size Deadpool #900 although the indicia for that issue left the "Team-Up" out of the title.

name: Emma Frost
desc: This series details Emma's early life and her time before the Hellfire Club and the manifestation of her powers.

name: Fantastic Four
desc: The series returned to it's original numbering after issue 14 of this series and ended with issue #645, seemingly ending the historic run of the Fantastic Four for the time being.

name: Ferals
desc: Blending elements of crime noir with classic monster horror, FERALS #1 begins with the personal tale of Officer Dale Chesnutt, a lawman in the sleepy town of Cypress. Folks are turning up not just dead, but slaughtered in bestial fashion.

name: Frankenstein
desc: Gothic horror in the macabre Marvel manner! One of the most terrifying figures in all of fiction lurches into his own 1970's comic book series. Witness a dramatic retelling of Mary Shelley's literary classic, then follow the Monster in his quest for the last living descendant of his creator, Victor Frankenstein. It's an odyssey that will lead him into a confrontation with Marvel's other groovy ghoulies, Dracula and Werewolf By Night!

name: Gotham Academy
desc: A comic book series published by DC Comics. The series takes place in the DC Universe's Batman mythos and follows Olive Silverlock, a teenage girl, and her friends as they encounter the mysteries and threats of Gotham's most prestigious prep school, Gotham Academy, which happens to be just across the road from the Arkham Asylum.

name: Justice League of America
desc: A New 52 title starring a new version of the Justice League of America recruited by director of A.R.G.U.S. Amanda Waller and led by A.R.G.U.S. member Steve Trevor, consisting of Green Lantern (Simon Baz), Martian Manhunter, Green Arrow, Stargirl, Catwoman, Hawkman, Katana and Vibe. It was later revealed that the League was assembled to combat the original Justice League, if it is ever required.

name: Midnight Tales
desc: An American horror-suspense anthology comic book series created by Wayne Howard that was published by Charlton Comics from 1972 to 1976.

name: New Avengers
desc: An All-New, All-Different Marvel series. An all new team of heroes under the leadership of ex-New Mutant Roberto DaCosta has taken up the name of the 'New' Avengers!

name: New Thunderbolts
desc:
Series is continued from Thunderbolts (1997) and the Avengers/Thunderbolts mini-series and continues in Thunderbolts (2006), going back to it's original numbering with issue 100.

Although this series has a new number 1, the original numbering is also visible, making this issue 82 - 99 of the Thunderbolts series.

name: Original Sin
desc: Nine issue event mini-series that follows a group of Marvel superheroes being lead by Nick Fury to figure out who killed Watcher and stole his eyes, which lead to many secrets of the Marvel universe to be exposed.

name: Shadowman
desc: There are a million dreams in the Big Easy. But now its worst nightmare is about to come true. As the forces of darkness prepare to claim New Orleans as their own, Jack Boniface must accept the legacy he was born to uphold. As Shadowman, Jack is about to become the only thing that stands between his city and an army of unspeakable monstrosities from beyond the night. But what is the true cost of the Shadowman’s otherworldly power? And can Jack master his new abilities before Master Darque brings down the wall between reality and the eldritch darkness of the Deadside?

name: Superboy
desc:
Numbering continues with The Adventures of Superboy #19.

Note: Volume named per indicia.

Superboy is the companion comic to the UPN series developed by Ilya and Alexander Salkind to follow their four Superman films. The series premiered October 8th, 1988. After John Byrne's The Man of Steel retconned Superman's career in Smallville as a boy out of the DCU Continuity.

This is Shuster University, in Seigel, Florida, student Clark Kent. Along with Lana Lang and T.J. White. TJ was later replaced with Andy McAllister. The series would feature some of the first live-action appearances of such classic rogues as Metallo and Mxyzptlk.

This book debuted February 1990, the same month as Second Season episodes Run, Dracula, Run; Brimstone; Abandon Earth and Escape To Earth. Seasons Three and Four shifted from Shuster University in Seigel, Florida to the Bureau of Extra-Normal Matters in Capital City, Florida. The reason for the Florida setting is the series was filmed at Disney/MGM, then Universal Studios in Orlando, Florida. The series ended with a final episode aired May 17, 1992. Time-Warner took control of Superboy back from the Salkinds. To date, only the John Haymes Newton, first season of the series has been released on DVD. The series was followed by Lois and Clark: The New Adventures of Superman, and later Smallville. This title would only survive two years and twenty-two issues, to February of 1992.

name: Talon
desc: A New 52 series, starring the Talon aka Calvin Rose, the only man to escape the fate of being the Court of Owls' master assassin.

name: Thanos
desc: A Marvel NOW! series. After Thanos' ordeal in the Infinity Revalation, Relativity and Finally, the Titan finds out he is dying.

name: Ultimate Avengers
desc: A comic book published by Marvel Comics that began in August 2009 as part of the relaunch of the Ultimate Universe under the "Ultimate Comics" imprint. It is a direct follow up to the events of "Ultimatum."

name: Unfollow
desc: A dying social media mogul leaves his billions to be split evenly between 140 random people—or however many of them are still alive at the moment of his death. Rob Williams (MARTIAN MANHUNTER, THE ROYALS: MASTERS OF WAR) and Michael Dowling (Death Sentence) assemble a cast that includes a young black man trying to get by in St. Louis, an Iranian reporter in need of hope, a retired special forces soldier with a strange sense of purpose, and a thrill-seeking heiress, in this thriller that shows we’re all still part of the food chain.

name: Young Liars
desc: The book centers around a group of 20-somethings in modern-day New York City, though the story quickly expands to other parts of America and the world. All of them have disturbing secrets about themselves that they keep from the others, and even the readers are left to decide what is true and what are lies.

name: All-Star Comics
desc: This series picks up numbering from the original All Star Comics (DC, 1940 series), ignoring the other series the numbering also continued in, All-Star Western (DC, 1951 series) #58-119.

name: The Amazing World of DC Comics
desc: DC Comics' self-produced fan magazine of the mid-1970s. Running 17 issues, the fanzine featured DC characters and their creators, and was exclusively available through mail order. Primarily text articles, with occasional strips and comics features, Amazing World offered a great deal of insight into Bronze Age DC corporate and creative culture.

name: Angel: After the Fall
desc: Set some time after the season 5 finale, "Not Fade Away", Los Angeles is feeling the aftermath of Angel taking a stand against the demonic Senior Partners, who have retaliated by literally sending the city to Hell. Along with a dragon he befriended, Angel is trying his best to remain a champion of good.

name: Frankenstein, Agent of S.H.A.D.E.
desc: One of The New 52 ongoing series published after Flashpoint. It was canceled with issue 16.

name: Generation Hope
desc: The series follows Hope and the Five Lights who are going on missions to help the other lights that are activating.

name: Hawkgirl
desc:
One Year Later than the events of INFINITE CRISIS, a new protector takes to the skies of St. Roch: Hawkgirl! Last seen in the depths of space, Hawkgirl is flying solo. But what has happened to Hawkman and will one Hawk be enough when their ancient enemy Hath Set comes into play?

NOTE: this series begins with issue #50.

name: Hawkman
desc: Hawkman and Hawkwoman battle the forces of evil on their new adopted home of planet Earth!

name: Justice League Quarterly
desc: A set of quarterly 80-page specials, supplementing the 1990's Justice League series.

name: Justice League United
desc: The team forms in the aftermath of "Forever Evil", following the disbandment of the United States Government-sanctioned Justice League of America.

associated.series: DC Sneak Peek: Justice League United (2015)

name: Legion Lost
desc: A New 52 volume featuring a group of Legion of Super-Heroes members stranded in the present day DCU.

name: Loki: Agent of Asgard
desc: Following Loki's adventures in Journey into Mystery and Young Avengers Vol. 2, the God of Mischief receives an All New Marvel NOW! ongoing series! The series was briefly replaced by a mini-series named Original Sin: Thor & Loki: The Tenth Realm that was set between issues 5 and 6 of this series.

name: The Metabarons
desc: A grand scale space opera about family, sacrifice, and survival told within an immense universe, both in scope and originality. A must-read cult spin-off of The Incal, by Moebius and Jodorowsky, centering around the fascinating lineage of the ultimate warrior. This collection introduces the Metabaron’s bloodline and reveals the origins of their deep-seated principles. Find out the source of the family’s vast wealth, learn why every Metabaron has cybernetic implants, and why the only way to become the next Metabaron is for him to defeat his own father in a mortal combat. Follow each successive generation as it struggles to overcome the forces amassed against it in a galaxy corrupted by greed, power, and terror. A true classic in the pantheon of graphic storytelling and Science Fiction as a whole.

name: Mind the Gap
desc: After Elle Peterssen is mysteriously attacked on a Manhattan subway platform, she is left in a coma, the only clues to her attacker trapped inside her mind. No one knows the identity of the person behind this brutal beating or where they will strike next. In this ALL-NEW ONGOING series, everyone is suspect, and no one is innocent.

name: Something Epic
desc: IMAGINATION IS REAL. Outside our perception, creative thought takes physical form, with only a handful of individuals known as Epics able to interact with this wondrous hidden world. But for fourteen-year-old Danny Dillon, accepting these responsibilities himself won't be easy-or safe. Lose yourself in a world of endless fantasy and creativity, where superheroes, monsters, magical creatures, and cartoon characters live and breathe alongside us. Fan-favorite SPAWN and Punisher artist SZYMON KUDRAŃSKI introduces a world where the only limitation is your imagination.

name: Spider-Woman
desc: An All-New, All-Different Marvel series. After the events of Spider-Woman Vol.4 and Secret Wars, Jessica Drew returns as Spider-Woman, and she is with child!

name: The Superior Foes of Spider-Man
desc: An ongoing comic book series published by Marvel Comics that debuted in July 2013. The series was written by Nick Spencer with artwork by Steve Lieber. It debuted as part of Superior Spider-Month which saw a major status quo change.

name: Thor
desc: Note: Cover title is "The Mortal Thor", but the indicia title "Thor". Legacy number became the indicia number from #800. Sigh...

name: Amethyst: Princess of Gemworld
desc: Following the adventures Amy Winston who attempts to resume the ordinary life of a 13-year-old on Earth all the while protecting her friends in the jeweled dimension!

name: Batman Beyond
desc: A new version of the Batman Beyond mythos starring Tim Drake taking up the beyond mantle, following the events of Futures End.

name: Bloodshot
desc:
Your name is Angelo Mortalli. Your brother is trapped behind enemy lines and on the verge of — no. That’s not right. Your name is Raymond Garrison. You’ve retired from the dangers of the field, but a desperate plea from your oldest friend plunges you into a vicious firefight that — no. That’s not right, either. You are Bloodshot. You are the shade of gray that freedom requires. The perfect confluence of military necessity and cutting-edge technology. A walking WikiLeaks. A reservoir of dirty secrets that could set the world on fire. And you’ve just been captured.

The title changes to 'Bloodshot and H.A.R.D. Corp' with issue #14, and reverts back with issue #24.

name: Dark Wolverine
desc: DARK WOLVERINE begins! Wolverine's son, Daken, has finally emerged from the shadows, stepping out onto the main stage of the Marvel Universe. As one of Norman Osborn's Avengers, he has power, access, and an identity that he hates--his father's. This new Wolverine doesn't know how long this will last, but one thing's for sure: He's going to have some fun while it does!

name: Doctor Who
desc: IDW Publishing brings The Eleventh Doctor to comics in this ongoing series. Spanning several story arcs, The Doctor along with companions Amy Pond and Rory Williams face everything from exploring the case of Jack the Ripper to fighting giant space squids. Find out what happens when they get between Vikings and Saxxons. Visit Casablanca, Run, Fight robot Santas, Run, Save the world and much much more.

name: Fear Agent
desc: After completion of The Last Goodbye and a one-shot "Tales of the Fear Agent: Twelve Steps in One," Dark Horse resumed chronological numbering for the series with number 17, making "The Last Goodbye" issues #12–15 and the one-shot #16.

name: Greek Street
desc: An American comic book series written by Peter Milligan with art by Davide Gianfelice. It retells and updates Greek myths. The series was canceled with issue #16.

name: Imperium
desc:
Ongoing series focusing on supervillain Toyo Harada trying to conquer and save the world or how Harada himself likes to call it, "The Battle for Utopia."

Continued from Harbinger: Omegas (and Harbinger).

name: Iron Man
desc: The title on the cover for issues #1-12 is "The Invincible Iron Man". The title on the cover for issues #15-16 is "Iron Man: Director of S.H.I.E.L.D.". Series continues after #16 as "The Invincible Iron Man".

name: Kurt Busiek's Astro City
desc: Numbering continues with Kurt Busiek's Astro City v3 #16 published by DC Comics.

name: Legion of Super-Heroes
desc: Legendary Legion writer Paul Levitz returns to the future with the Legion of Super-Heroes!

name: Mage
desc: Note: Indicia list title as "Mage". However, #11 and #12 have indicia title as "Mage: The Hero Defined" before reverting back to "Mage" for the final 3 issues of the series.

name: Punisher
desc: After his family was massacred by the mob, Frank Castle vowed to avenge them by exterminating all criminal vermin.  Emerging as the Punisher and armed with an arsenal of weapons, this lone soldier is ready to clean up the streets once and for all!

name: Secret Avengers
desc: A Marvel NOW! title. The Secret Avengers are revived when S.H.I.E.L.D. Agents Nick Fury Jr. and Phil Coulson put together a covert ops Avengers team that includes Black Widow, Hawkeye, Hulk and Winter Soldier.

name: Special Marvel Edition
desc: The series started out as a reprint series before telling new Shang-Chi stories.

name: Superman: The Man of Tomorrow
desc: A comic book series published by DC Comics that ran for 16 issues from 1995 to 1999, featuring the adventures of Superman. At the time, the four Superman titles (Action Comics, The Adventures of Superman, Superman, and Superman: The Man of Steel) were released weekly with an intertwining story. The Man of Tomorrow was created to fill the extra week in months with five weeks. At about this time, however, DC began its fifth week events, disrupting the schedule of The Man of Tomorrow, which was subsequently canceled with issue #15.

name: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Journeys
desc: Note: Indicia lists title as "Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Journeys", changed in idicia of Issue #2 to "TMNT: Journeys"

name: Thor
desc: Odinson once more claims the name of Thor, God of Thunder! And just in time, for he is the only hope in stopping the War of the Realms.

name: Wolverine Weapon X
desc: An ongoing Wolverine series by Jason Aaron telling tales of Wolverine that aren't necessarily apart of any other series' continuity.

name: All-New, All-Different Avengers
desc: Spinning out of the pages of Avengers Vol.5 and Secret Wars comes an all-new team of Avengers.

name: All-New Invaders
desc: An All New Marvel NOW! series. The famed superhero team from World War Two returns in the present day to fight the evils that have been lurking in the shadows since the end of the second world war.

name: The Authority
desc: The Authority returns and they now have Jenny Quantum-the Spirit of the 21st Century on their side!

name: Birds of Prey
desc: This second volume of Birds of Prey was launched under the Brightest Day umbrella of titles and featured the return of fan-favorite writer Gail Simone. She reunited the Birds of Prey team from her original run and added Hawk and Dove to the regular cast.

name: Black-Eyed Kids
desc: It's dark. You're alone. Then there's a knock. You open the door to find two seemingly normal kids. They ask to come in, to borrow your phone to call for a ride. You find yourself overcome with an intense fear that you can't explain. And then you notice their eyes... black... SOLID black. You want to run, but now they're inside. It's too late. They have you. Eisner Award winner Joe Pruett (X-Men Unlimited, Cable) is joined by artist Szymon Kudranski (Spawn, Penguin: Pain and Prejudice) for this terrifying new horror series.

name: Black Panther
desc: After the Black Panther's stint in Jungle Action, the African hero stars in his very own magazine, drawn and written by the legendary Jack Kirby!

name: Books of Magick: Life During Wartime
sort_name: Books of Magick: Life During Wartime
desc:
A fantasy comic book series published by DC Comics under their Vertigo imprint in 2004 and 2005 that was discontinued after fifteen issues.

The series depicts the events that take place on two fictional worlds, both of which are connected through an alternate version of the character Timothy Hunter.

name: Captain Britain and MI:13
desc: The Skrull Invasion isn’t restricted to the US. When the Skrull Invasion hits England, only Captain Britain and MI: 13 stand in their way, but repelling this threat comes at a price. Now all kinds of magical evil has been released across Britain and its up to Captain Britain and Pete Wisdom's MI: 13 to stop it.

name: Doctor Strange
desc: The series was continued from Strange Tales Vol.1 #168. It lasted until issue 183 after which the series was cancelled.

name: Doctor Who: The Eleventh Doctor
desc: This is one of three ongoing Doctor Who comics by Titan Comics in the US. It uses British creative talent despite being intended for American audiences. This volume and Doctor Who: The Tenth Doctor launched in July 2014, with Doctor Who: The Twelfth Doctor following a few months later after Peter Capaldi's first full season started airing on TV. The three comics were later combined into one title for sale in UK newsagents in February 2015, called Doctor Who Comic.

name: Doctor Who: The Twelfth Doctor Year Two
sort_name: Doctor Who: The Twelfth Doctor Year Two
desc: The Golden Years of the Doctor and Clara begin, as the Twelfth Doctor comics leap into Series 9! Writer Robbie Morrison is back with a year-long extravaganza that kicks off with an excellent jumping-on point for new readers - while Rachael Stott (Star Trek) joins us as new regular series artist!

associated.series: Doctor Who: The Twelfth Doctor Year Three (2017)

name: Earth X
