desc: A 1999 comic book limited series published by American company Marvel Comics. Earth X was written by Jim Krueger with art by John Paul Leon. Based on Alex Ross' notes, the series features a dystopian version of the Marvel Universe.

name: The Forged
desc: This series takes place during the 11th Millenium under the reign of the Empress Eternal and follows Forged Team Scimitar-3, a team of Super Soldiers who find themselves caught in a strange conspiracy during what they think is a routine mission.

name: Green Arrow
desc: This new series follows after Green Arrow / Black Canary and the events in Justice League: Cry for Justice and Justice League: Rise and Fall.

name: Injection
desc: An American comics ongoing series, created in 2015 by Warren Ellis and illustrated by Declan Shalvey and Jordie Bellaire, who previously collaborated on Ellis's Moon Knight run for Marvel Comics. The comic is high-concept science fiction fused with elements of magic and mythology, and also invokes British literary and pop cultural archetypes, such as Bernard Quatermass, Sherlock Holmes, Doctor Who, James Bond and Carnacki.

name: The Official Handbook of the Marvel Universe
sort_name: Official Handbook of the Marvel Universe
desc: An encyclopedic guide which details the fictional universe featured in Marvel Comics publications. The original 15-volume series was published in comic book format in 1982, followed by sporadic updates.

name: RASL
desc:
Jeff Smith, the visionary writer and artist behind the epic fantasy Bone and Shazam: Monster Society of Evil, unveils his newest series, the stark sci-fi series, Rasl!

Meet Rasl, an art thief searching for his next big score - and trying to escape his past! Where other thieves plan their heists with breathtaking precision, Rasl has an ace up his sleeve - he can travel through the light between dimensions, affording him access to museums that no ordinary thief could access!

Smith's first major independent work since the critically acclaimed and award-winning Bone is 32 pages long per issue.

name: Red Sonja
desc: The first ongoing Red Sonja series. The series was a continuation from the Marvel Feature series that starred Red Sonja as well.

name: Secret Avengers
desc: A new start for the covered-ops Avengers team! Continued directly from Secret Avengers vol. 2.

name: The Silver Coin
desc: The narrative revolves around a single, mysterious silver coin, marked by an eerie engraving of a goat’s eye. The object passes from hand to hand across various historical eras, from the distant, Puritan New England of 1492 to a desolate cybernetic future in 2467. Anyone who comes into possession of the coin initially sees their deepest desires fulfilled or gains a prodigious talent: a failed rock band from 1978 experiences sudden success, a young girl bullied at camp finds a way to redeem herself, and a desperate gambler begins winning every hand. However, the coin carries a ruthless, sentient curse that demands a blood tribute; every fleeting stroke of luck quickly turns into a claustrophobic and violent nightmare, leading the unfortunate owners toward tragic and grotesque ends.

name: Skyward
desc: Skyward is an adventure-filled exploration of our world turned upside down and a young woman’s journey to find her place in it.

name: Squadron Supreme
desc: An All-New, All-Different Marvel series. The Squadron's first ever ongoing series! Out of the ashes of the Secret Wars mini-series comes a new Squadron set in the main Marvel Universe!

name: Stars and S.T.R.I.P.E.
desc: The series that kicked off Geoff Johns' DC career and introduced Courtney Whitmore, the Star Spangled Kid! When Courtney discovers her stepfather was the sidekick of the Star-Spangled Kid, she begins acting as the all-new Star-Spangled Kid! He retaliates by donning an 8-foot suit of armor to keep her out of trouble, and adventure ensues!

name: Young Avengers
desc: A Marvel NOW! series written by Kieron Gillen and illustrated by Jamie McKelvie and Mike Norton.

name: 1001 Arabian Nights: The Adventures of Sinbad
sort_name: 1001 Arabian Nights: The Adventures of Sinbad
desc: Some call him a womanizer others call him charismatic, some think him a brute others charming but all know one thing – Sinbad is a serious bad-ass! Zenescope Introduces a Sinbad series that will reinvent the legend. When Sinbad is unjustly accused of murder and banished from his home city, he learns there is one artifact that might be able to clear his name, but the quest to find it is certainly not an easy one. From beautiful women to terrifying creatures to armies of blood thirsty villains, this is one epic fantasy/adventure series that will hook you in and not let go.

name: Action Philosophers!
desc: ACTION PHILOSOPHERS! is a comic book series detailing the lives and thoughts of history's A-list brain trust in a hip and humorous way that proves that philosophy is not just the province of boring tweed-enveloped college professors.

name: Age of Apocalypse
desc: Spinning directly out of UNCANNY X-FORCE! The Amazing X-Men have lost and the evil Weapon X is more powerful than ever! But who are these heroes, these lowly mortal men and women, who step out from the shadows? Who are the X-Terminated?

name: Batman: Dark Victory
desc: Even in the aftermath of THE LONG HALLOWEEN, Batman finds no peace. Gotham City is caught in the middle of a battle between what's left of the Falcone mob and freakish villains such as the Joker, Mr. Freeze and Catwoman.

name: Danger
desc:
Anthology series. Originally adventure themed but switched to espionage/spy themed issues and featured Duke Douglas character. Issues #1-5 bear the tagline, "Men Without Fear" and the rest have "Secret Agents...Spies...Espionage...Intrigue"

Issues #1-11 were published by Comic Media
Issues #12-14 were published by Charlton

name: Free Planet
desc: Following a grueling war of independence, the newly liberated world of Lutheria becomes the first completely free planet in human history. A volatile faction of revolutionary heroes, known as the Freedom Guard, is tasked with protecting the planet's vital energy resources from invading intergalactic superpowers. However, as political deadlock, resource shortages, and civil unrest threaten to tear their fragile new society apart, the heroes must confront their own wildly conflicting visions of what true freedom actually entails.

name: Inhuman
desc: After the events of Infinity and the Inhumanity mini-series, a new breed of Inhumans is born all over the world. Follow these NuHumans in an exciting and all new ongoing series, produced by the top writer and art-teams of today! The series was concluded in a big Inhuman Annual. This series also span a second new ongoing series, The Uncanny Inhumans. The series also had an Inhuman Special one-shot.

name: Invincible Iron Man
desc: Preceded by the Superior Iron Man series. After the events of Secret Wars, Tony Stark returns to the true hero he was, as the Invincible Iron Man!

name: Iznogoud
desc: 14 issue series which is an English translation of Les Adventures du Grand Vizir Iznogoud.

name: Mighty Avengers
desc: A Marvel Now title. The title features the street-level Avengers under the leadership of Luke Cage.

name: Paradise X
desc:
A 14 issue limited series.

Note: Issue #X is labeled in indicia as "Paradise X: X Vol. 1 No. 1", with a different barcode sequence. However, this is being treated as an aberration as the primary story from this miniseries follows directly from issue #12 to issue #X, the cover style does not indicate a change, and the covers of all issues including #X combine to create a single image.

name: Secrets of Sinister House
desc: A horror-suspense anthology comic book series published by DC Comics from 1972–1974, a companion to Forbidden Tales of Dark Mansion. Both series were originally inspired by the successful ABC soap opera Dark Shadows, which ran from 1966 to 1971.

associated.series: The Sinister House of Secret Love (1971)

name: Superman Confidential
desc: A series that featured Superman stories set in the early years of the character’s career. The stories illustrated key moments in the character’s past such as first meetings, critical decisions, alliances, confrontations, and events that shaped him into the character he is today. The creative team on the series rotated.

name: The Twelve
desc: An American comic book limited series from Marvel Comics, which the company announced in July 2007 would run twelve issues beginning spring 2008, with the creative team of writer J. Michael Straczynski and artist Chris Weston. The series stars 12 obscure superheroes from Marvel's earliest incarnation as Timely Comics from the 1940s period historians and fans call the Golden Age of Comic Books.

name: Wrath of the Eternal Warrior
desc: Ongoing series focusing on Gilad's immortality and what happens when he's dying and coming back to life.

name: X-Treme X-Men
desc: An ongoing series written by Greg Pak and drawn by Stephen Segovia, Paco Diaz and Andre Araujo starring a ragtag team of X-Men from alternate Earth.

name: 1st Issue Special
desc: 1st Issue Special was a comics anthology series from DC Comics, done in a similar style to their Showcase series. It was published from April 1975 to April 1976. The goal was to showcase a new possible first issue of an ongoing series each month, with some issues debuting new characters and others reviving dormant series from DC's past. No series were actually launched from 1st Issue Special but the Warlord made his first appearance in the title and the character's ongoing series was already slated to debut a few months later.

name: Alone
desc:
Thirteen issue series. 

These are English translations of a French series titled "Seuls."

name: Aquaman
desc: Aquaman has lost everything he holds dear--his wife, his child, his kingdom--and is now an obsessed man, driven by non-stop super-heroics as the King of the Seven Seas. He's a man who keeps his pain inside, allowing his anger and sorrow to emerge in violent action!

name: The Astonishing Ant-Man
desc: An All-New, All-Different Marvel series. The series was a direct continuation of the Ant-Man Vol. 1 series and the Ant-Man: Last Days one-shot.

name: Avengers vs. X-Men
desc: It's no longer coming, it's here! Does the return of the Phoenix on Earth signal the rebirth of the mutant species or the end of life as know it? And when the Avengers and X-Men end up on opposing sides, it means war!

name: Batman: The Long Halloween
desc: Written by Jeph Loeb (SUPERMAN/BATMAN, Heroes) with art by Tim Sale (SUPERMAN FOR ALL SEASONS) and set during Batman's early days, this acclaimed series focuses on a killer murdering only on holidays. Batman must races against the calendar to discover who Holiday is before they claim more victims!

associated.series: Batman: The Long Halloween: The Last Halloween (2024)

name: Black Hammer
desc: Series follows a team of heroes who vanished in the middle of a cataclysmic battle and found themselves trapped in a small town they were incapable of leaving.

name: The Daring New Adventures of Supergirl
sort_name: Daring New Adventures of Supergirl, The
desc:
Series starring Supergirl (Kara Zor-El).

Note: Issue 13 has just "Supergirl" on the cover but the indicia is still "Daring New Adventures of Supergirl".

name: Doctor Who: The Eleventh Doctor Year Three
sort_name: Doctor Who: The Eleventh Doctor Year Three
desc: Same great creators – whole new flavor! The Eleventh Doctor begins his blockbuster third year with writer Rob Williams (Suicide Squad) and series artists Simon Fraser and Leandro Casco in the hot seat!

sort_name: Doctor Who: The Twelfth Doctor Year Three
desc: Fan-favorite comics companion (and space bassist of the far future) Hattie returns for a story involving nightmarish denizens of the deep, shambling seaweed, creepy British seaside towns, and the best fish and chips of the 1970s!

associated.series: Doctor Who: The Twelfth Doctor Year Two (2016)

name: Doktor Sleepless
desc: This originally ongoing series from writer Warren Ellis went on hiatus after computer problems destroyed the author's notes for future storylines in 2009. Future issues were announced and delayed over the next several years, and eventually the series was conceded to have ended without concluding the story.

name: Exquisite Corpses
desc: Set against the dark backdrop of the underworld, the story follows a desperate investigator who delves into a web of conspiracy, murder, and deception following a high-profile execution. As hidden motives surface and alliances shift, the protagonist must navigate a lethal labyrinth of criminals and corrupt figures to uncover the truth before becoming another body in the pile.

name: Fantastic Four
desc: This series takes place in the "Heroes Reborn" Universe created by Franklin Richards after the Onslaught story arc.

name: Fearless Defenders
desc: Misty Knight and Valkyrie take center stage as the Fearless Defenders! A series that is somewhat continued from Fear Itself: The Fearless. Despite the name, the team featured are not the Defenders and are instead a team of Valkyrior, later established to be the Lady Liberators.

alt_names: The Flash: The Fastest Man Alive
desc:
Indicia titles are:

* #6-13 - The Flash: The Fastest Man Alive

name: Iron Man
desc: Continues the adventures of Iron Man following the Onslaught Saga event. Part of Marvel's Heroes Reborn crossover event.

name: Jughead: The Hunger
desc: Jughead: The Hunger is a comic book series published by Archie Horror, an imprint of Archie Comics, beginning in 2017. The story, which takes place in its own continuity, focuses on Jughead Jones and his family's dark legacy to explain the sinister origin of his hunger.

name: Mass Effect: Foundation
desc: Thirteen-part maxiseries revolving around Maya Brooks, the villain of Mass Effect 3's "Citadel" DLC, and her behind-the-scenes experiences with each member of the Normandy's crew during her service with Cerberus.

name: The Mighty Crusaders
desc:
Note:

Indicia title for issues #4 - #13: The Mighty Crusaders

name: Not Brand Echh
desc:
satiric comic book series published by Marvel Comics that parodied its own superhero stories as well as those of other comics publishers. Running for 13 issues (cover-dated Aug. 1967 to May 1969), it included among its contributors such notable writers and artists as Stan Lee, Jack Kirby, Gene Colan, Bill Everett, John and Marie Severin, and Roy Thomas. With issue #9, it became a 68-page, 25¢ "giant", relative to the typical 12¢ comics of the times.

Its mascot, Forbush Man, introduced in the first issue, was a superhero wannabe with no superpowers and a costume of red long johns emblazoned with the letter "F" and a cooking pot, with eye-holes, covering his never-revealed head. His secret identity was eventually revealed in issue #5 (Dec. 1967) as Irving Forbush, Marvel's fictitious office gofer.

name: Quantum and Woody
desc:
Once upon a time, Eric and Woody Henderson were inseparable. Adopted brothers. Best friends. Brilliant minds. Years later, they are estranged siblings, petty rivals, and washed-up failures. But when their father's murder leads them into the throes of a life-altering scientific accident, Eric and Woody will find themselves with a whole new purpose - and a perfectly legitimate reason to wear costumes and fight crime.

Even as a kid Woody was always the black sheep of his adopted family, constantly getting in to trouble and dragging his brother, Eric, down with him. The two are forced to reunite as adults to investigate their father's mysterious death. While investigating their father's laboratory, the two are given superpowers when a piece of lab equipment explodes, but the powers come with a price: they must KLANG! their bracers together periodically or be ripped apart.

Now ex-military Eric Henderson must put up with his not-quite reformed conman brother as they attempt to find justice for their father and make a little profit on the side.

name: The Ravagers
desc: A The New 52 title, featuring a group of young teen heroes known as the Ravagers.

name: Shaman's Tears
desc: The comic starred Joshua Brand, the son of a half-Sioux father and an Irish mother, who returns as an adult to the reservation he ran away from as a child. Discovering he mystically possesses the powers of all animals and the Earth itself, he becomes the protector of the planet. The book often dealt with ecological and animal rights issues.

name: Venom: Space Knight
desc: An All-New, All-Different Marvel series. From his adventures in Guardians of the Galaxy comes Flash Thompson and Venom in an all-new series.

name: 2020 Visions
desc: A science fiction comic book written by Jamie Delano and drawn by four artists. Originally serialized as a twelve-issue full-color limited series from 1997 to 1998 at the Vertigo imprint of DC Comics

name: Agents of Atlas
desc: After the Agents of Atlas mini-series, the team got its very own ongoing series.

name: All Star Superman
desc:
A twelve-issue American comic book series featuring Superman that was published by DC Comics. The series ran from November 2005 to October 2008. The series was written by Grant Morrison, drawn by Frank Quitely, and digitally inked by Jamie Grant. The series revolves around Superman, who is dying due to overexposure to the Sun, as he accomplishes many heroic feats (The Twelve Labors of Superman) and attempts to make peace with the world before his imminent death.

The origin of the series started with Morrison's desire to tell a "timeless" Superman story that wasn't an origin story or followed a classic narrative. Morrison originally planned a revamp of the Superman character, titled "Superman Now", but after the approach was declined, decided they wouldn't write anything related to Superman until DC Vice President Dan DiDio contacted them. Some of the ideas planned for "Superman Now" were subsequently reused for All-Star Superman.

The series was the second to be launched in 2005 under DC's All-Star imprint, the first being All Star Batman & Robin, the Boy Wonder. These series were attempts by DC to allow major comics creators a chance to tell stories showcasing these characters without being restricted by DC Universe continuity. All-Star Superman received overwhelming critical acclaim for its emotional story, characterization, writing, and artwork, and is considered to be one of the best Superman stories and one of the greatest comic books of all time.

Note: The first issue shows "All-Star Superman" in the indicia, the rest are all "All Star Superman".

name: Amazing Detective Cases
desc: Twelve issue mini-series. Series issue number continues from a pulp magazine by the same title.

name: Amethyst: Princess of Gemworld
desc: For twenty years the evil Dark Opal has reigned and ruled Gemworld. However unbeknownst to him a sorceress for the Amethyst monarchy hid away the young princess.Now on earth she has turned 13 years old. When she is called forth she is a twenty year old woman. Can she bring forth a new age to Gemworld. Can she figure out her powers in the course of this twelve issue maxi-series ? Can she defeat Dark Opal.

name: Army @ Love
desc:
An American comic book series from DC Comics' Vertigo imprint, which started in May 2007. It is drawn and scripted by Rick Veitch, with Gary Erskine on inking duties. Issue #12 published in February 2008 was the "season finale".

The story follows the adventures of a unit of New Jersey National Guard in "Afbaghistan", a fictional Middle Eastern country.

name: The Authority: Revolution
desc: They’ve saved Earth from annihilation over and over again. Now they want to rule the world…

name: Avengers A.I.
desc: The series takes place after the events of Age of Ultron, where the world has been colonized by A.I.s "who may or may not have positive feelings about the way humanity has been treating them for the past 100 years."

name: Avengers Forever
desc: A time-spanning saga stretching through several ages of the mighty Marvel Universe.

name: A Walk Through Hell
desc:
So these two FBI agents walk into a warehouse…

Special Agents Shaw and McGregor handle the routine cases nowadays, which is just the way Shaw likes it. She’s pushing 40, a borderline burnout, the ghastly memories of her last investigation still clinging like shadows. McGregor is younger, more dedicated, hanging onto some measure of idealism whatever the world might throw at him.

When two fellow agents go missing inside a Long Beach warehouse, Shaw and McGregor are sent to investigate. But what they find waiting is far from routine, as the local police have already discovered to their cost. Before the night is out, our heroes will encounter terror beyond their most appalling nightmares—in a place where the night may never end at all.

A new kind of horror story for modern America, written by Garth Ennis (Preacher, The Boys, Crossed) and drawn by Goran Sudžuka (Y: The Last Man, Hellblazer)

name: Batman and Robin: Year One
desc:
A 12-issue limited series.

Note: The indicia list the title as "Batman and Robin: Year One," which differs from the cover dressing.

name: Black Canary
desc: Seattle is coming apart, and only one hero can hold it together. Dinah Lance takes on the criminal underground as the Black Canary in her very own solo series!

name: Black Panther
desc: Continued from Black Panther Volume 4. A new Black Panther takes the lead, but... who is she?

name: Blade Runner 2019
desc: In the neo-noir city of Los Angeles, 2019, Ash, a veteran Blade Runner, is grappling with a new case: a billionaire's wife and child, apparently kidnapped by Replicants for dark purposes... An all-new ongoing comic series from the pen of Academy Award-nominated screenwriter Michael Green (Blade Runner 2049, Logan, American Gods), with longtime co-writer Mike Johnson (Batman/Superman, Supergirl, Star Trek), illustrated by Andres Guinaldo (Justice League Dark, Captain America). The first comic to tell original, in-canon stories set in the Blade Runner universe!

name: Blade Runner 2029
desc: A series of 12 issues and a sequel to Blade Runner 2019 and followed by Blade Runner 2039.

name: Blood Squad Seven
desc: In the 1990s, Blood Squad Seven was the ultimate strike team of government-sanctioned superheroes, dominating the tactical landscape and pop culture before vanishing after a disastrous secret mission. Decades later, a new generation is assembled to revive the legendary franchise, but they must navigate lethal covert ops, corporate branding, and the dark, unresolved secrets left behind by the original team.

name: Camelot 3000
desc: 12 issue maxi-series from writer Mike W. Barr and artist Brian Bolland. The series was one of DC's first maxi-series to be targeted for the Direct Market comic book stores.

name: Crisis on Infinite Earths
desc: Literally all the greatest DC Universe heroes from across time and space join forces to stop a being more powerful than any they've ever faced! But with existence crumbling around them, this may be a fight that no one walks away from. Don't miss the classic story that altered the DCU forever!

name: The Dead Lucky
desc: San Francisco resident Bibi Gomez is a former soldier suffering from PTSD who survived a catastrophic platoon wipeout in Afghanistan. Left with the ability to see and control electrical energy, as well as a pair of terrifying, ghost-like mechanical titans that follow her, Bibi returns home to find her neighborhood overrun by a mercenary police force and criminal gangs. Taking up the vigilante identity of The Dead Lucky, she uses her strange powers and battle armor to fight for her community while unraveling the mystery behind her unit's destruction.

name: Deadpool Corps
desc: When tapped by the Elders of the Universe to gather a crack team of his alternate universe selves, Deadpool can’t say no and the Deadpool Corps is born.

name: Defenders
desc: Spinning out of the stunning end of FEAR ITSELF! Everyone's favorite Marvel characters banding together to solve a mysterious conspiracy deep at the heart of the Marvel Universe!

name: Doctor Who: Prisoners of Time
desc:
The Doctor is an alien, the last of the powerful Time Lords of the planet Gallifrey. He is an intrepid traveller through time and space, armed with an incredible intelligence. He travels alone except for the human companions he befriends, briefly sharing his life with them and showing them the astonishing wonders of the universe.

50th anniversary maxi-series.

name: Doom Patrol
desc: The sixth volume of Doom Patrol and the first to be released under DC's Young Animal imprint, serving as the flagship title of the line.

name: Doomsday Clock
desc: DC Comics presents to you a 12-issue maxi-series from the critically acclaimed team of writer Geoff Johns, artist Gary Frank and colorist Brad Anderson. You are not prepared for what lies ahead within these pages, good readers.

name: Dragonlance: Chronicles
desc: Twelve issue series. The cover says Dragonlance Chronicles Dragons of Spring Dawning. However, the indicia makes mo mention of the subtitle.

name: The Fade Out
desc: Charlie Parish, a Hollywood screenwriter suffering from PTSD, is fronting for his blacklisted best friend, Gil. When Charlie wakes from a blackout in the same room as a murdered starlet, he and Gil set out to bring her killer to justice.

name: The Flash
desc: The new Flash series that spins out of Brightest Day, starring Barry Allen as the Flash.

name: The Flintstones
desc: The first family of Bedrock (and civilization, really) tells the story of who we are and why we do what we do as if it all began with Fred, Wilma, Barney, Betty and the rest of the citizens of Bedrock. Shining a light on humanity's ancient customs and institutions in a funny origin story of human civilization, Mark Russell (PREZ) blends modern interpretations with Hanna-Barbera's classic character's, bringing a breath of fresh stone-age air.

name: Freedom Fighters
desc:
Line up for this all-new maxi-series set on Earth X, where the Nazis won World War II! Twenty years after invading and occupying America, Germany wiped out all meta-human resistance, including the original Freedom Fighters.

Fast-forward to the present day, and a new team of Freedom Fighters emerges to challenge the Nazi occupation once again. But if they’re to have any chance of victory, they’re going to need Uncle Sam—who disappeared after his original team was killed. The 12-part epic “Death of a Nation” story-line kicks off here!

name: Generation X
desc: After the events of Inhumans versus X-Men, a new group of mutants enroll in the Xavier Institute for gifted youngsters.

name: Hard Time
desc: A comic book series written by Steve Gerber and Mary Skrenes and originally published by DC Focus, a short-lived imprint of DC Comics. The aim of the imprint was to feature super-powered characters who did not follow the traditional format of classic superhero adventures. Hard Time's first run was 12 issues long, published from April 2004 to March 2005.

name: Honor and Curse
desc: Orphaned as a young boy, Genshi Sakagura was adopted by the Iga clan after witnessing the murder of his parents. Now, Genshi is a promising young shinobi with dreams of marrying Lord Haruki’s beautiful daughter, Akemi, and leading the Iga clan warriors into battle. Genshi’s future was promising, until his past came back to torment him in the form of an evil mountain spirit known as a Tengu. This demon relentlessly haunts Genshi’s dreams and bends reality around him, but nothing compares to when the Tengu consumes him; Genshi transforms into an unstoppable force of nature incapable of remorse!

name: Hulk
desc: The Hulk stars in his own new series. It is a direct continuation of The Incredible Hulk (Vol.2) that had ended the month before with issue 474. The series lasted for 11 issues and was renamed as The Incredible Hulk (Vol.3) with issue 12.

name: Incredible Hulk
desc: Continued from the second “adjectiveless” Hulk Vol.2 series. 13 issues of that series were published under the guise of “The Incredible Hul” series. After 13 issues of that volume, “The Incredible Hulk” series reached it's 600th issue and returned to it's original numbering and name. It continues with yet another title change starting with issue 612, namely Incredible Hulks.

name: The Inhumans
desc: From the pages of the Fantastic Four come the Inhumans in their own series! The most uncanny heroes of all! The race known as the Inhumans star in their first own ongoing series. It was a bi-monthly series that lasted for 12 issues.

name: Inhumans
desc: A new Inhumans series, starting out as a new ongoing series along with a bunch of other new 'manga styled' comics under the Marvel imprint known as the "Tsunami Line". Unfortunately, along with many of the other Tsunami comics, it failed to catch an audience and was cancelled with issue 12.

name: The Invincible Iron Man
desc: Numbering continues from “Iron Man (2005)” and after #28 it becomes “Iron Man: Director of S.H.I.E.L.D. (2008)”.

name: Invincible Universe
desc: A series featuring characters from the Invincible Universe which lasted for 12 issues.

name: Ivar, Timewalker
desc: At this very moment in Geneva, Switzerland, history is being made. A thousand meters underground inside the Large Hadron Collider, researcher Neela Sethi is about to discover time travel – and jeopardize her life in the process. But she doesn’t know that yet. Ten minutes from now, every deadbeat chrononaut, wannabe conqueror, and misguided protector of the timestream will be banging down her door. Good thing that the legendary Ivar, Timewalker, got there first…right? Now it’s down to history’s most jaded, most tempestuous time traveler to stop the worst of everything that is, was, and will be…before time runs out!

name: JLA: Year One
desc: Five of the world's greatest heroes come together to save the world from a crisis of global proportions. They are the Justice League of America--and this is the story of their re-imagined origins and first year in the DCU.

name: Justice League Elite
desc: Members of the Justice League join with members of the Elite to form a task force willing to take on the darker and grittier missions of the world.

name: Justice League International
desc: A new ongoing starring the Justice League International written by Dan Jurgens with art by Aaron Lopresti.

name: The Kamandi Challenge
desc:
In honor of the 100th birthday of Jack "The King" Kirby, some of today's greatest comics creators are throwing down a one-of-a-kind challenge to one another to create the most breathtaking, mind-blowing story the world has ever known. This is The Kamandi Challenge!

Kamandi, Jack Kirby's beloved post-apocalyptic Last Boy on Earth, fights for his survival and the fate of all humankind in a world overrun by intelligent tigers, giant robot leopards, edible plant people and even more wonders. 

But this is no ordinary comics story. Each all-star creative team leaves Kamandi in a death-defying cliffhanger, and it's up to the next storytellers to pick up the gauntlet and figure out how Kamandi will survive! The result is a wild comics ride that's worthy of the King himself!

Take up the challenge and see how a combination of comics legends and today's best creators--including Tom King (Batman), Neal Adams (Green Lantern/Green Arrow), James Tynion IV (Detective Comics), Bill Willingham (Fables), Amanda Conner and Jimmy Palmiotti (Harley Quinn), Ivan Reis (Justice League), Walter Simonson (Orion) and more--set out the ultimate challenge for their fellow creators!

name: Legion Lost
desc: Their future is lost! Upon preventing a cataclysmic rift in their universe, several members of the 30th century's famed Legion of Super-Heroes find themselves stranded from home--with no safe return! Writing duo Dan Abnett and Andy Lanning bring readers a new chapter in the legend of the Legion!

name: Marvel 2-in-One
desc: A classic title from Marvel's storied history is back at last — and it's fantastic! With Reed and Sue Richards gone and presumed dead, Johnny Storm and Ben Grimm reunite in a bid to find their new place in the Marvel Universe.

name: Marvel Feature
desc: A small series with a large legacy; It features the formation and first appearance of the Defenders.

name: Marvel Presents
desc: A short-lived series featuring the first appearance of Bloodstone and the further adventures of the Guardians of the Galaxy.

name: Nextwave: Agents of H.A.T.E.
desc: Nextwave is a high action superhero comic that is a parody of high action superhero comics.

name: Nightcrawler
desc: An All-New-Marvel Now title. The return of Chris Claremont to one of his most famous creations, Nightcrawler.

name: Orchid
desc: This series is planned out to be a 12 issue Maxi-series with Tom Morello scripts and Scott Hepburn interiors.

name: Royals
desc: Twelve issue series starring the Inhumans. Spinning form the pages of the ongoing Uncanny Inhumans series and the Inhumans Prime one-shot.

name: Shang-Chi

name: She-Hulk
desc: With a new practice, a new paralegal and a mounting number of super villains she's racking up as personal enemies, She Hulk might have bitten off a little more than she can chew...but she just calls that that Tuesday.

name: Sheriff of Babylon
desc: A twelve-issue American comic book first published by Vertigo Comics in 2015. Sheriff was created by Tom King and Mitch Gerads.

name: Sidekick
desc: What happens when a beloved hero who committed crimes unknown to those closest to him for selfish reasons, fakes his death and leaves his Sidekick with nothing? Flyboy learns the hard way as he realizes the only thing good in his life was being the Red Cowl's sidekick. Add in a little manipulation from a villain and we see Flyboy's life spiraling down the wrong path.

name: Sleeper
desc: Secret Agent Holden Carver is a man on a mission -- only nobody left alive seems to know it.

name: Solo
desc: An American comic book series that was published bi-monthly by DC Comics, beginning in October 2004. Each issue had 48 pages plus covers, with no ads.

name: Space Ghost
desc: The 2025 Space Ghost Vol. 2 comic series from Dynamite Entertainment focuses on Space Ghost and his sidekicks, Jan, Jace, and Blip, facing escalating dangers within the Galactic Federation, culminating in a looming galactic war against a council of classic villains led by the mysterious Time Master.

name: Superior Spider-Man Team-Up
desc: After Doctor Octopus became the Superior Spider-Man, the team-up book Avenging Spider-Man was rebooted as Superior Spider-Man Team-Up.

name: U.S. 1
desc: A Marvel Comics comic book series that debuted in 1983. The series was produced based on a license of the US-1 Trucks slot truck toyline from Tyco Toys.

name: U.S.Avengers
desc: A Marvel NOW! series. The team that was formed in the pages of New Avengers Volume 4 comes together once more with a few new additions to the team. The series ends with issue 12, but the teams journey continues in Avengers issue 675, in which the "No Surrender" story-line starts, combining 3 Avengers teams in one series.

name: Watchmen
desc:
Watchmen is Alan Moore's seminal comic series. It has been proclaimed one of the greatest literary works ever created and was the only comic book to be featured in Time Magazine's best 100 English-Language novels from 1923 to present.

"Who watches the Watchmen?" This slogan was everywhere: on the Universal Product Code box of direct market comics; adorning the bottoms of letter columns, and in provocative full page house ads. DC knew it had its hands on something truly great, and it wanted to whet the appetite of as many fans as it possibly could. When the first part of the 12 issue maxi series, "Watchmen" hit the stands, readers weren't quite sure what they were going to get. But when word of mouth began to spread about both the quality of Alan Moore's scripting and Dave Gibbons' detailed drawings, "Watchmen" became a fast seller and a fan favorite.

The writer had originally intended for his opus to chronicle the future of the fondly remembered heroes from the defunct publisher Charlton Comics. However, DC soon decided it had its own plans for those heroes and so Moore created new characters to give "Watchmen" its own distinctive universe. The story itself is a masterful example of comic book storytelling at its finest. As the obsessive Rorscharch began to investigate the murder of his old teammate the Comedian, a mysterious conspiracy unraveled that both saved the world and damned it. Filled with symbolism, foreshadowing and ahead-of -its-time characterization thanks to adult themes and sophisticated plotting, "Watchmen" elevated the super hero comic book into the realms of modern literature.

name: Wolverine & the X-Men
desc: Continued from Wolverine & the X-Men Vol.1. School's back in session. But where are the teachers?

name: Young X-Men
desc: In the wake of Messiah CompleX, there are no X-Men and young mutants are alone and directionless.

name: All-New Inhumans
desc: An All-New, All-Different Marvel series. Continuing the story from the Inhuman Vol. 1 and The Uncanny Inhumans Vol. 1 series, comes this new adventure!

name: All Select Comics
desc: An American comic book series published by Timely Comics, the 1940s predecessor of Marvel Comics, during the period fans and historians call the Golden Age of comic books. An omnibus series with several different superhero and other features each issue, it primarily starred Captain America and the original Human Torch, two of Timely's most popular characters, as well as fellow Timely star the Sub-Mariner in several.

name: American Vampire: Second Cycle
desc: Following the conclusion of "The Blacklist," Scott Snyder and Rafael Albuquerque's hit series American Vampire came to a close, and went on hiatus for over a year.

name: Battlestar Galactica: Origins
desc: DYNAMITE ENTERTAINMENT continues their successful run of Galactica "origins" with an all new series focusing on the characters and events of the award-winning Sci Fi series!

name: Cloak and Dagger
desc: After their popular mini-series from 1983, Cloak and Dagger got their own ongoing series written by Bill Mantlo.

name: C.O.W.L.
desc: The "Chicago Organized Workers League" -- the world's first Super-Hero Labor Union!

name: Death Or Glory
desc: Meet Glory: a young woman raised off the grid in a convoy of truckers, the last men and women fighting for true freedom on the American open road. Now, in order to pay for her dying father’s surgery, Glory has three days to pull off four dangerous cross-country heists with mob killers, crooked cops, and a psycho ex-husband all out to bring her in—or die trying. New York Times bestselling author RICK REMENDER teams up with legendary French superstar BENGAL to bring you a high-speed chase across the American West that examines our dwindling freedoms, and the price of fighting for an untethered life

name: Drax
desc: Drax the Destroyer, former member of the Infinity Watch and current member of the Guardians of the Galaxy stars in his own ongoing series.

name: Escape
desc: SHOT DOWN. HUNTED. OUT OF TIME. Set in a brutal, fully painted world of anthropomorphic animals—equal parts Inglourious Basterds and Watership Down— ESCAPE is a gritty, bullet-riddled journey through war’s scorched aftermath. It’s about the violence we inflict, the souls we try to save, and the courage it takes to crawl out of fire. From the creative team of New York Times bestselling author RICK REMENDER (DEADLY CLASS, Uncanny X-Force) and powerhouse DANIEL ACUÑA (Captain America, Black Panther)—the duo behind Marvel’s Uncanny Avengers—comes a savage, full-throttle wartime thriller where survival isn’t given… it’s taken.

name: Fear Agent
desc: Fear Agent is an American science fiction comic book series written by Rick Remender with art by Tony Moore and Jerome Opena, who alternated on story arcs. The  first volume was by Image Comics from 2005-2007.

name: Final Boss
desc: When a virtual game turns into reality, humanity is driven to the brink of destruction. Xia Ye always thinks he is a noob, but he is actually the final boss of the game's story, who is so incredibly powerful that even the fearless warriors fear him.

name: Hulk
desc: After the events of Civil War 2, Jennifer Walters is no longer She-Hulk, but known as simply the Hulk! After issue 11, the Marvel Legacy event starts, in which the series is renamed She-Hulk and all of the issues of the previous volume's of She-Hulk are counted together, making the 12th issue the 159th in total.

name: Jean Grey
desc: The young time-displaced Jean Grey has visions of the Phoenix coming for her. As such, she tries to gain knowledge and power to face the Phoenix head-on!

name: Namor: The First Mutant
desc: Marvel's first mutant, Namor the Sub-Mariner divides his time between ruling the undersea kingdom of Atlantis and fighting for equality on the surface as a member of the X-Men. Can even the Avenging Son prove up to such daunting tasks? He certainly thinks so!

name: Phantom Lady
desc: After Quality stopped publishing the adventures of Phantom Lady, what was now simply Iger Studios believed it owned the character and assigned it to Fox Feature Syndicate, a move that would later cause confusion as to who actually owned the character's copyright. The Fox version which premiered in Phantom Lady #13 (taking over the numbering of Wotalife Comics) is better known to contemporary comic fans than the Quality version because of the "good girl art" of Matt Baker. Baker altered her costume by changing the colors to red and blue, substantially revealing her cleavage, and adding high-cut loose shorts.

name: Private Dance
desc:
Private Dance takes you into a New York strip club as we meet the dancers, customers, and bouncers, discovering that there is more to the fantasy than meets the eye.

At work, they create a fantasy for customers that you have to see to believe. However, when we take a closer look, there is a world of stories to explore in the real lives of these dancers.

name: Sea of Stars
desc: Being a space trucker sounds like a cool job, but in reality, it can be boring as hell. So when recently widowed Gil gets a long-haul gig across the universe, he figures it’s safe enough to bring his young son Kadyn along for the ride—that is, until their “big rig” gets bitten in half by a gigantic Space Leviathan! Now separated from his son—with a breached suit that’s venting oxygen at an alarming rate—Gil must defy the odds and stay alive long enough to rescue Kadyn. But meanwhile, Kadyn seems to be getting all the help he needs from a talking Space Monkey riding a Space Dolphin… or maybe it’s the strange powers he’s suddenly manifesting?!

name: Secret Empire
desc: From the pages of Captain America: Steve Rogers, comes the ultimate betrayal of one of the Marvel's biggest heroes! Captain America has become an agent of Hydra and will take America by storm!

name: Transformers: Generation 1
desc: Vol. 3 of Transformers: Generation 1 series from Dreamwave comics, but the first ongoing series. It was canceled when Dreamwave went bankrupt.

name: Transformers Timelines
desc:
Timelines is comic book series by Fun Publications where they publish their Transformers fiction. The stories are released in conjunction with BotCon and the Transformers Collectors' Club. Stories are contain both original timelines as well as build on existing continuities.

Note: in 2014 Fun Publications included the original Transformers Timelines #1 - Descent into Evil into their numbering resulting in that years issue being #10 instead of #9. Issue #9 was released later as a digital exclusive comic.

name: X-Men: Red
desc: A new chapter of the X-men begins in this series starring the newly ressurected Jean Grey as she forms her own group of X-Men and fights Cassandra Nova.

name: A-Force
desc: An All-New, All-Different Marvel series. A team of female heroes takes charge! After the Sercret Wars tie-in A-Force Volume 1, a new ongoing series starts set in the Main Marvel Universe. The series lasted for only 10 issues.

name: Afterlife with Archie
desc:
Afterlife with Archie is a comic book published by Archie Comics beginning in 2013, depicting a zombie apocalypse that begins in the town of Riverdale in an alternative reality. It is written by Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa, with art by Francesco Francavilla, and is inspired by a zombie-themed variant cover which Francavilla did for an issue of Life with Archie.

The comic is Archie Comics' first title to be sold only on the direct market (that is, in comic shops), as opposed to on newsstands; it is also the company's first title not to be aimed at children and is rated "TEEN+", as it includes content and subject matter never explored in any previous Archie title, including extensive realistic violence, some gore, necrotic themes, disturbing scenes, and moderate language. The comic was conceived not long after Archie Comics officially dropped the Comics Code Authority standard from their entire line-up in 2011.

Issue #8 was the first to feature the company's Archie Horror logo.

name: Avengers: No Road Home
desc: Night has fallen across the universe. Now seven Avengers - and one new addition - journey forth to bring back the light. But when the threat they face has destroyed even the Gods...will anyone make it home?

name: Baker Street
desc: Baker Street features an alternative Sherlock Holmes world where the values and class system of Victorian era England carried over into a late 20th century where World War II never occurred.

name: Black Road
desc: A Viking comic book series written by Brian Wood and published by Image Comics, with art by Garry Brown. Set during the Viking Age in Norway, it follows the story of the main character, Magnus the Black.

name: Crossed
desc: Garth Ennis has pulled out all the stops to write the most depraved and twisted book of his career, one that also may be his most poignant human drama! Crossed is Ennis' horrifically visceral exploration of the pure evil that humans are truly capable of indulging and collected here are all ten heart-stopping chapters. This gut-wrenching vision is brought to vivid (and more than a little disturbing) life by his partner in crime Jacen Burrows. Imagine, for a moment, the worst crimes against humanity. Picture the cruelest affronts to decency. Conjure your darkest nightmares... and then realize it could all be so much worse. When civilization crumbles in one terrifying moment; when people are gleefully breaking into unthinkable acts of violence all around you; when everyone you love has died screaming in agony: What do you do? There is no help. There is no hope. There is no escape. There are only the Crossed.

name: Daytripper
desc:
Daytripper is a comic book series from Vertigo that focuses on the life of Bras de Oliva Domingos at different ages in his life. Each issue deals with a separate issue in life, ranging from being overshadowed by the work of his parents to the birth of his first child, and how precious each of these moments are in one's life. Unfortunately, Bras never gets to enjoy those moments, as the series runs a gimmick that features Bras de Oliva Domingos dying at the end of each issue.
Most commonly, Bras de Oliva Domingos is portrayed as a writer of some sort, mainly an obituarist but occasionally as an author of books. From issue to issue, other characters that have shown up in previous issues will appear in the issue directly following it as some role in Bras' life.

name: D'Orc
desc:
The story takes place in the fantasy world of Sunderaine, caught in an endless war between Light and Darkness (elves versus orcs, wizards versus common sense, dragons versus everyone).

The protagonist is a lonely and hapless orphan who is half dwarf and half orc: D’Orc. A troubling apocalyptic prophecy hangs over him, designating him as the destroyer of the world, destined to bring an end to that eternal conflict. For this reason, creatures from every faction—humans, elves, goblins, giants, and monsters of all kinds—want him dead. D’Orc travels armed only with a magical, sentient, and strangely violent shield that craves combat, finding himself in the midst of crazy and grotesque situations (including a chicken-headed ghost).

name: Grumble
desc: Tala’s mother had told her plainly, if you’re ever in trouble, find Eddie. He can help you. So, she did just that when she was pursued by the S’Taera -- interdimensional beings who believed Tala did not properly observe the “purity” of magic. Tala found Eddie hustling cards and embarrassing himself. Maybe mother doesn’t always know what’s best?

name: I Heart Skull-Crusher!
desc: Originally solicited as a 5 issue limited series, it became a short-lived ongoing series, which finished at #10.

name: The Killer
desc: THE KILLER, a hardboiled 10-issue noir series chronicling one man’s journey through some seriously bad mojo.

name: Kull, the Conqueror
desc: The series changed it's name and continues in 'Kull, the Destroyer' with issue #11.

name: The Mighty Captain Marvel
desc: A Marvel NOW! series. Series ends with #9 and continues with Captain Marvel (2017) #125

name: Napalm Lullaby
desc: Fifty years after a god-like superpowered entity crash-landed on Earth and established a brutal, theocratic dictatorship, humanity lives under strict totalitarian control. The story follows two estranged, illegitimate children of this miraculous tyrant—each possessing unpredictable, dangerous powers—who emerge from the destitute slums to infiltrate the domed fortress-city of adulation and assassinate the immortal father who ruined their world. A series that lasted for 10 issues.

name: Omega the Unknown
desc: Omega the Unknown was created by Steve Gerber and Mary Skrenes. The series told the story of one of Marvel's most unique heroes, the mysterious Omega. This ahead-of-its-time series however failed to catch on and ended with issue 10, but remains a cult classic. Although the series ended with issue 10, Omega's story was continued in issues 75 (prelude) 76 and 77 and 78 (epilogue) of The Defenders series.

name: Spider-Woman
desc: An all-new series starring the original Spider-Woman, Jessica Drew. Follow Spider-Woman during and after the events of Spider-Verse.

name: Supergirl
desc: Continues the numbering from the previous "The Daring New Adventures of Supergirl" series.

associated.series: The Daring New Adventures of Supergirl (1982)

name: West Coast Avengers
desc: Kate Bishop starts up her own team of Avengers, with some help from the original Hawkeye, Clint Barton.

name: American Carnage
desc: A new, thrilling crime saga from the writer of WILDSTORM: MICHAEL CRAY and the artist of The Old Guard! Disgraced FBI agent Richard Wright is offered a chance for redemption when his old mentor sends him undercover to infiltrate a white supremacist group believed to be responsible for the death of a fellow agent.

name: Battlefields
desc:
Nine issue mini-series. This is known as Battlefields volume 1.

* "The Firefly and His Majesty" story arc (Issues #4-6) are the sequel to "Battlefields: The Tankies" (2009) #1-3
* "Motherland" story arc (issues #7-9) are the sequel to "Battlefields: The Night Witches" (2008) #1-3

name: Batwoman
desc:
The series picks up with Kate Kane attempting to escape the cycle of violence and mysticism that has defined her life since childhood.  The story begins with Kate in Greece, a setting intended to highlight the "Soldier" aspect of her character while leaning into the "ghosts" of her past.

The central conflict revolves around the Religion of Crime and the "prophecy" that has haunted Kate since she was ten years old.  Greg Rucka has described the initial arc as an "exorcism," intended to resolve narrative threads he has been considering for nearly seventeen years.  The tone is described as a supernatural-noir thriller that asks the question: "How do you fight the devil when the devil is real—and how do you win?"

name: Captain America and Bucky
desc: Starting with issue #629, the title became Captain America and Hawkeye, shifting it to a team-up series.

name: Deathstroke: The Terminator
desc:
After years of operating as a mercenary and superhuman assassin-for-hire, Slade Wilson finds himself the prey rather than the predator.  A mysterious enemy from his past has begun a systematic campaign to dismantle his life piece by piece, destroying his resources, allies, and reputation.

The series follows Slade as he "evolves into his purest form" - a relentless terminator driven by raw vengeance.  Decoupled from the usual superhero drama, the story explores the dark world of professional assassins within the DC Universe, promising a "bloodier than ever" crusade that rivals the intensity of a hard-boiled crime thriller.

name: Devil Dinosaur
desc: Witness the legend of Devil Dinosaur. Residing deep in the Valley of the Flame, Devil Dinosaur forms an unlikely bond with Moon-Boy. Is the red-skinned and red-eyed Dino as menacing as the town-folk believe?

name: Heroes In Crisis
desc: Heroes in Crisis is a nine issue series that deals with the emotional cost of being a superhero and will explore "what violence does to a society",

name: Incredible Hulk
desc: Ongoing series continuing from The Totally Awesome Hulk with Legacy numbering. The series restarts (but also has the Legacy numbering) with a new number 1 in The Immortal Hulk, in which Bruce Banner returns to life.

name: John Byrne's Next Men
desc: John Byrne and the Next Men return. The original series debuted in 1992 and ended in 1994. The next chapter in the lives of the survivors of Project Next Men are all here. This is where the action begins.

name: Lobo
desc: "The Main Man" is back to his classic, unfiltered roots, embarking on a "guts-soaked" journey across the DC Universe.  The story follows Lobo as he barrels toward the very end of the universe with a singular, chaotic mission: to scratch his name and number into the Source Wall with a "cool knife."

name: The Phantom Stranger
desc: Following the eighth issue, the series was retitled Trinity of Sin: The Phantom Stranger, to reflect the naming of Trinity of Sin: Pandora.

associated.series: Trinity of Sin: The Phantom Stranger (2013)

name: Sword of Sorcery
desc: Amethyst returns! Amy Winston has grown up on the road with her mother. Their life is strange, and it only gets weirder when she discovers she's the lost princess of Gemworld--and has powerful enemies hunting her!

name: 30 Days of Night: Bloodsucker Tales
desc:
Eight issue series.

In Bloodsucker Tales, Steve Niles continues the saga of 30 Days of Night with the bloody and terrifying story "Dead Billy Dead," illustrated by talented newcomer Kody Chamberlin. Matt Fraction (Last of the Independents) joins in with "Juarez," introducting Lex Nova, former private detective and free-range madman, illustrated by Ben Templesmith.

name: Adam Strange
desc:
Andy Diggle reinvented a classic character with the Vertigo hit Swamp Thing… now, teamed with Pascal Ferry (Action Comics, Tom Strong), Diggle sets his sights on DC's premiere science-fiction hero: Adam Strange!

In this action-packed 8-issue miniseries, things have changed drastically for Strange. Once the greatest hero of the distant planet Rann, he’s now a wanted man on Earth. Pursued by the police and hunted by aliens, Strange has learned that his adopted planet has been destroyed. With his wife and daughter gone, is there any hope left, or is this the end of the space hero?

Sit back for a thrilling ride that takes one man on a trek though the DC Universe to rediscover the remnants of the L.E.G.I.O.N., the Darkstars, the Omega Men, and more as he faces a threat that will herald a galactic war!

name: Angel + Spike
desc: Eight issue series. Issue numbering is a continuation from Angel (2019) series, so it begins with issue #9

name: A Nightmare on Elm Street
desc: A Nightmare on Elm Street was the first of New Line's horror titles to be published by Wildstorm, with Friday the 13th and The Texas Chain Saw Massacre following in 2007. The opening story arc introduced a new group of teens for Freddy Kruger to hunt, including Jade Arnstrum, who had witnessed Freddy killing her brother in a dream. With her father's help, Jade attempted to save her friends from Freddy and rescue a comatose girl from his dreamworld. Chuck Dixon's script and Kevin J. West's pencils helped to create a suitably nightmarish start for Freddy's latest incarnation.

name: The Atom & Hawkman
desc: When sales of both Atom & Hawkman were on the slide, the two comics combined, continuing number wise where the Atom left off. Running for 7 issues, the comic sometimes featured our heroes in a team up and at other times they were in separate adventures. Continues from The Atom volume 1.

name: Blackhawks
desc: A "The New 52" initiative book starring the technologically advanced military force, The Blackhawks.

name: Black Summer
desc: The world goes black in Warren Ellis' epic story of super-powered heroes and villains. The story begins when the political situation in the USA becomes more than Horus can stand, and he moves to take matters into his own hands. Unfortunately, not all of his other team-mates are quite so eager to throw the world into chaos, and an epic conflict forms. With Horus and the rest of the surviving Guns facing off against the military and each other, no one is safe as the bodies start to fall.

name: Black Widow
desc: Natasha Romanova is one of Marvel's foremost female Avengers and a talented super-spy. She's gone toe to toe with Marvel's most powerful villains and has fought alongside some of the most valiant heroes. As the Black Widow she knows how to get the job done right. Black Widow is an action-packed comic filled to the brim with international espionage, intrigue and one of the most daring women in comics today!

name: Blue & Gold
desc:
An eight issue mini-series starring Blue Beetle and Booster Gold.

Note: Indicia lists title as 'Blue & Gold'.

name: Countdown to Adventure
desc: Spinning out of the pages of the critically acclaimed yearlong weekly series 52, Adam Strange, Animal Man and Starfire have returned to their respective homes, but where do they go from there? Plus, a backup tale tying into COUNTDOWN TO FINAL CRISIS!

name: Daredevil: End of Days
desc: An American comic book miniseries featuring the Marvel Comics character Daredevil, written by Brian Michael Bendis and David W. Mack, drawn by Klaus Janson, inked by Bill Sienkiewicz and with covers by Alex Maleev. Mack, Sienkiewicz and Maleev also contribute occasional interiors and splash pages throughout the series. It concerns the death of Daredevil, not unlike previous "Marvel: The End" miniseries, which told the final stories of other Marvel Comics characters.

name: Death of the New Gods
desc: Writer and artist Jim Starlin helmed this eight issue series as a mysterious force brought destruction to the inhabitants of the Fourth World.

name: Doctor Who: Ghost Stories
desc:
Digital first eight issue mini-series.
Also available in print, Doctor Who: Ghost Stories.

name: Dragonlance: Chronicles
alt_names: Dragonlance Chronicles: Dragons of Autumn Twilight
desc: Eight issue series. The inside covers say "Dragonlance: Chronicles - Dragons of Autumn Twilight" but the indicia makes no mention of the subtitle

name: Eternal Warrior
desc:
Gilad Anni-Padda, The Eternal Warrior, gets his own ongoing solo series as part of the Summer of Valiant Year 2.

Across ten millennia and a thousand battlefields, Gilad Anni-Padda has traversed the darkest, most mysterious corners of history. But the horror and bloodshed of constant warfare has finally taken its toll on the man myth calls the Eternal Warrior…

name: Falcon
desc: From the pages of Captain America: Sam Wilson comes a hero renewed! Sam Wilson is back as the Falcon, and nothing will ever be the same!

name: The Ghost Fleet
desc: The series was originally supposed to be twelve issues. However, after initial sales were below expectations that was cut to eight issues and the final four issues were only ever released on the publishers digital platform.

name: G.I. Combat
desc: G.I. COMBAT reimagines characters from DC's classic war properties for the 21st century--and beyond!

name: G.I. Joe
desc: Originally expected to be twelve issues. It was cut short and concluded at eight.

name: Guardians of Infinity
desc: An All-New, All-Different Marvel series. After their adventures in Guardians 3000 and the Secret Wars Korvac Saga tie-in series, the Guardians of the 31st Century return in their own ongoing series!

name: Hawkeye
desc: The first Hawkeye ongoing series. From carnival roustabout to petty thief to trouble-making hero, one thing about ex-Avenger and Thunderbolt Clint Barton has never changed: he's a sucker for a lost cause. His travels in search of the world's best chili take Hawkeye out of spandex and into the real world problems of real world losers.

name: House of M
desc: The Avengers and the X-Men are faced with a common foe that becomes their greatest threat: Wanda Maximoff! The Scarlet Witch is out of control, and the fate of the entire world is in her hands. Will Magneto help his daughter or use her powers to his own benefit?
